title.zh: 卷一百六十 列傳第四十七: 王磐 王鶚 高鳴 李冶 李昶 劉肅 王思廉 李謙 徐世隆 孟祺 閻復
title.en: Volume 160 Biographies 47: Wang Pan, Wang E, Gao Ming, Li Ye, Li Chang, Liu Su, Wang Silian, Li Qian, Xu Shilong, Meng Qi, Yan Fu
title.raw: 卷一百六十 列傳第四十七: 王磐 王鶚 高鳴 李冶 李昶 劉肅 王思廉 李謙 徐世隆 孟祺 閻復 Volume 160 Biographies 47: Wang Pan, Wang E, Gao Ming, Li Ye, Li Chang, Liu Su, Wang Silian, Li Qian, Xu Shilong, Meng Qi, Yan Fu

sentences.zh: 王磐字文炳，廣平永年人，世業農，歲得麥萬石，鄉人號萬石王家。

translations.literal: Wang Pan, style name Wenbing, was a man of Yongnian in Guangping. His family farmed for generations; each year they harvested ten thousand shi of wheat, and the villagers called them the Ten-Thousand-Shi Wang Family.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pan, courtesy name Wenbing, came from Yongnian in Guangping. For generations his family worked the land and harvested ten thousand shi of wheat a year, so locals nicknamed them the "Ten-Thousand-Shi Wangs."

sentences.zh: 父禧，金末入財佐軍興，補進義副尉。

translations.literal: His father Xi, at the end of the Jin, contributed wealth to assist military efforts and was appointed Assistant Commander of Advance Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi, in the closing years of the Jin, donated funds to support the war effort and received appointment as Assistant Commander of the Advance Righteousness unit.

sentences.zh: 國兵破永年，將屠其城，禧復罄家貲以助軍費，衆賴以免。

translations.literal: When the state army took Yongnian and was about to slaughter the city, Xi again exhausted the family fortune to assist military expenses, and the multitude relied on this to escape.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mongol army captured Yongnian and prepared to massacre the city, Xi once more poured out the family wealth to help pay military costs, and the townspeople owed their survival to him.

sentences.zh: 金人遷汴，乃舉家南渡河，居汝之魯山。

translations.literal: When the Jin people moved to Bian, the family as a whole crossed the river south and dwelt at Lushan in Ru.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin court moved its capital to Bian [Kaifeng], the whole household crossed south over the Yellow River and settled at Lushan in Ru prefecture.

sentences.zh: 磐年方冠，從麻九疇學于郾城，客居貧甚，日作糜一器，畫為朝暮食。

translations.literal: Pan had just come of age when he studied under Ma Jiuchou in Yancheng; as a lodger he was extremely poor, making one pot of gruel a day and dividing it for morning and evening meals.
translations.idiomatic: Pan had only just reached manhood when he studied with Ma Jiuchou in Yancheng. Living there as a guest, he was desperately poor: each day he cooked a single pot of gruel and divided it between morning and evening meals.

sentences.zh: 年二十六，擢正大四年經義進士第，授歸德府錄事判官，不赴。

translations.literal: At age twenty-six he was selected in the fourth year of Zhengda as a metropolitan graduate in Classics and Meaning, appointed Registrar and Adjudicator of Guide Prefecture, but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-six he passed the metropolitan examination in Classics and Meaning in the fourth year of Zhengda, was named Registrar and Adjudicator of Guide Prefecture, and declined the post.

sentences.zh: 自是大肆力於經史百氏，文辭宏放，浩無涯涘。

translations.literal: From then on he devoted great effort to the classics, histories, and the hundred schools; his literary style was broad and unrestrained, vast without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he threw himself into the classics, histories, and the hundred schools of thought. His writing was expansive and free, seemingly boundless.

sentences.zh: 及河南被兵，磐避難，轉入淮、襄間，宋荊湖制置司，素知其名，辟為議事官。

translations.literal: When Henan suffered warfare, Pan fled for refuge, moving between the Huai and Xiang regions; the Song Jing-Hu Pacification Commission, which had long known his name, recruited him as a deliberation officer.
translations.idiomatic: When war ravaged Henan, Pan fled and drifted between the Huai and Xiang regions. The Song Jing-Hu Pacification Commission, already familiar with his reputation, appointed him as a policy adviser.

sentences.zh: 丙申，襄陽兵變，乃北歸，至洛西，會楊惟中被旨招集儒士，得磐，深禮遇之，遂寓河內。

translations.literal: In bingchen [1236], after the mutiny of troops at Xiangyang, he returned north; reaching west of Luoyang, he met Yang Weizhong, who had been ordered to gather Confucian scholars; obtaining Pan, he treated him with deep respect, and Pan lodged at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1236, after the mutiny at Xiangyang, he went north again. West of Luoyang he met Yang Weizhong, who had been ordered to gather scholars; Yang received Pan with great honor, and Pan took up residence at Henei.

sentences.zh: 東平緫管嚴實興學養士，迎磐為師，受業者常數百人，後多為名士。

translations.literal: Yan Shi, regional commander of Dongping, established schools to nurture scholars and received Pan as teacher; students regularly numbered in the hundreds, and many later became eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi, the regional commander of Dongping, founded schools to cultivate talent and welcomed Pan as his teacher. Students often numbered in the hundreds, and many later became celebrated figures.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，即拜益都等路宣撫副使，居頃之，以疾免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was immediately appointed Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Yidu circuit and others; after a short time he was excused on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1260 he was promptly appointed Vice Pacification Commissioner for Yidu and neighboring circuits, but soon resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 李璮素重磐，以禮延致之，磐亦樂青州風土，乃買田渳河之上，題其居曰鹿菴，有終焉之意。

translations.literal: Li Tan had long esteemed Pan and invited him with ceremony; Pan also delighted in Qingzhou's climate and soil, bought land above the Mi River, titled his dwelling Deer Hermitage, and had the intention of ending his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tan had long admired Pan and invited him with full courtesy. Pan also loved Qingzhou's landscape, bought land along the Mi River, named his home Deer Hermitage, and intended to live out his days there.

sentences.zh: 及璮謀不軌，磐覺之，脫身至濟南，得驛馬馳去，入京師，因侍臣以聞。

translations.literal: When Tan plotted rebellion, Pan perceived it, escaped to Jinan, obtained relay horses and galloped away, entered the capital, and had it reported through attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan plotted treason, Pan sensed it, slipped away to Jinan, seized relay horses, and raced to the capital to alert the court through the emperor's attendants.

sentences.zh: 世祖即日召見，嘉其誠節，撫勞甚厚。

translations.literal: The Founder summoned him the same day, praised his loyal integrity, and comforted and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai summoned him that same day, praised his loyalty, and treated him with exceptional warmth and reward.

sentences.zh: 璮據濟南，大軍討之，帝命磐參議行省事。

translations.literal: Tan held Jinan; the great army campaigned against him, and the emperor ordered Pan to deliberate on metropolitan administration affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With Tan holding Jinan, the imperial army marched against him, and the emperor appointed Pan to advise the metropolitan administration.

sentences.zh: 璮平，遂挈妻子至東平。

translations.literal: When Tan was pacified, he then brought wife and children to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: After Tan's defeat, he moved his wife and children to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 召拜翰林直學士，同修國史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Direct Academician of the Hanlin, jointly compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy and helped compile the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 出為真定、順德等路宣慰使。

translations.literal: He went out as Pacification Commissioner of Zhending, Shunde, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Pacification Commissioner for Zhending, Shunde, and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 衡水縣達魯花赤忙兀，貪暴不法，縣民苦之。

translations.literal: Mangwu, darughachi of Hengshui County, was greedy, violent, and lawless, and the county people suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: Mangwu, the Mongol overseer of Hengshui County, was greedy and brutal; the people suffered greatly under him.

sentences.zh: 有趙清者，發其罪，既具伏矣，適初置監司，其妻懼無以滅口，召家人飲酒至醉，以利啗之，使夜殺清，清逃獲免，乃盡殺其父母妻子。

translations.literal: A man named Zhao Qing exposed his crimes; he had already confessed fully. Just as supervisory offices were first established, Mangwu's wife feared there would be no way to silence witnesses; she summoned household members, got them drunk with wine, bribed them with profit, and had them kill Qing by night. Qing fled and escaped, so they killed all his parents, wife, and children.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Zhao Qing exposed Mangwu's crimes, and Mangwu had already confessed. When new supervisory offices were set up, Mangwu's wife feared witnesses would talk. She got her household drunk, bribed them, and sent them to kill Zhao Qing by night. Qing escaped, so they murdered his entire family—parents, wife, and children.

sentences.zh: 清訴諸官，權要蔽忙兀，不為理，又欲反其具獄。

translations.literal: Qing appealed to the officials, but powerful figures shielded Mangwu and would not hear the case; they also wished to reverse the completed conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qing appealed to the authorities, but powerful patrons shielded Mangwu. Officials refused to act and even tried to overturn the closed case.

sentences.zh: 磐竟奏置諸法，籍其家貲，以半給清。

translations.literal: Pan ultimately memorialized to apply the full penalty, register his household property, and give half to Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Pan finally secured a memorial sentencing Mangwu under the law, confiscating his estate and awarding half of it to Zhao Qing.

sentences.zh: 郡有西域大賈，稱貸取息，有不時償者，輒置獄于家，拘繫榜掠。

translations.literal: In the prefecture was a great merchant from the Western Regions who lent money for interest; when borrowers did not repay on time, he would imprison them in his house, detain them, and flog them.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy merchant from the Western Regions in the prefecture made loans at interest. When borrowers missed payments, he locked them in his house and beat them.

sentences.zh: 其人且恃勢干官府，直來坐廳事，指麾自若。

translations.literal: The man also relied on influence to interfere with government offices, coming straight in to sit in the council hall and command affairs as if at home.
translations.idiomatic: He also used his connections to bully officials, walking into the yamen hall, taking a seat, and ordering people about as if he owned the place.

sentences.zh: 磐大怒，叱左右捽下，箠之數十。

translations.literal: Pan was greatly angered, shouted for attendants to drag him down, and flogged him several tens of strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Pan flew into a rage, ordered his men to drag the merchant down, and had him beaten dozens of times.

sentences.zh: 時府治寓城上，即擠諸城下，幾死，郡人稱快。

translations.literal: At the time the prefectural seat was lodged atop the city wall; he was immediately pushed off the wall, nearly dying, and the people of the prefecture rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural offices were then housed atop the city wall; Pan had the man thrown over the parapet. He nearly died, and the whole prefecture cheered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，蝗起真定，朝廷遣使者督捕，役夫四萬人，以為不足，欲牒鄰道助之。

translations.literal: Before long locusts arose in Zhending; the court sent an envoy to supervise extermination with forty thousand laborers, deemed insufficient, and wished to memorialize neighboring circuits for assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon locusts swarmed Zhending. The court sent an envoy to supervise eradication with forty thousand laborers, judged that insufficient, and wanted to draft neighboring circuits for help.

sentences.zh: 磐曰：「四萬人多矣，何煩他郡！」

translations.literal: Pan said: "Forty thousand men are already many—why trouble other prefectures!"
translations.idiomatic: Pan said, "Forty thousand men are already plenty—why bother other circuits?"

sentences.zh: 使者怒，責磐狀，期三日盡捕蝗，磐不為動，親率役夫走田間，設方法督捕之，三日而蝗盡滅，使者驚以為神。

translations.literal: The envoy was angry, blamed Pan in a report, and set a three-day deadline to exterminate all locusts. Pan was unmoved, personally led laborers into the fields, established methods to supervise extermination, and in three days the locusts were entirely destroyed; the envoy was astonished and regarded it as miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was furious, filed charges against Pan, and gave him three days to eliminate every locust. Unshaken, Pan led the workers into the fields himself, organized an effective campaign, and wiped out the plague in three days. The envoy was astounded and called it miraculous.

sentences.zh: 復入翰林為學士，入謁宰相，首言：「方今害民之吏，轉運司為甚，至稅人白骨，宜罷去之，以蘇民力。」

translations.literal: He returned to the Hanlin as Academician, paid respects to the chief minister, and first said: "Among officials who harm the people today, the Transport Office is worst, even taxing human bones—it should be abolished to revive the people's strength."
translations.idiomatic: Back in the Hanlin as an academician, he visited the chief minister and said first, "Among today's oppressive officials, the transport commissioners are the worst—they tax people to the bone. Abolish the office and let the people breathe."

sentences.zh: 由是運司遂罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Transport Office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The transport offices were abolished as a result.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬諷大臣，請合中書、尚書兩省為一，拜右丞相安童為三公，陰欲奪其政柄。

translations.literal: Ahmad prompted the great ministers to request merging the Central Secretariat and the Department of State Affairs into one, appointing Right Chancellor Antong as one of the Three Dukes, secretly wishing to seize his political power.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad urged senior ministers to merge the Central Secretariat and the Department of State Affairs, elevate Right Chancellor Antong to the rank of Three Dukes, and thereby quietly strip him of real authority.

sentences.zh: 有詔會議，磐言：「合兩省為一，而以右丞相緫之，實便，不然，則宜仍舊，三公既不預政事，則不宜虛設。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered discussion; Pan said: "Merging the two departments into one under the Right Chancellor would indeed be convenient; otherwise the old arrangement should remain. Since the Three Dukes do not participate in government affairs, they should not be set up in vain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a debate. Pan argued, "If the two departments are merged under the Right Chancellor, that may work—but otherwise keep the old system. The Three Dukes do not govern; there is no point creating empty titles."

sentences.zh: 其議遂沮。

translations.literal: The proposal was then thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme was blocked.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿，乞致仕，不允。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and requested retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, he asked to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 時宮闕未建，朝儀未立，凡遇稱賀，臣庶雜至帳殿前，執法者患其諠擾，不能禁。

translations.literal: At the time the palace had not been built and court ritual was not established; whenever congratulations were offered, officials and commoners mixed before the tent hall, and law officers worried about the clamor but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The palace was still unfinished and court ceremony unsettled. At congratulatory audiences, officials and commoners crowded the tent hall, and guards could not keep order.

sentences.zh: 磐上疏曰：「按舊制：天子宮門，不應入而入者，謂之闌入。

translations.literal: Pan submitted a memorial saying: "According to old regulations: at the Son of Heaven's palace gates, one who should not enter but does is called forcible entry.
translations.idiomatic: Pan memorialized: "Under the old rules, anyone who enters the Son of Heaven's gates without authorization commits forcible entry.

sentences.zh: 闌入之罪，由第一門至第三門，輕重有差。

translations.literal: The crime of forcible entry, from the first gate to the third gate, had differing severity.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties for forcible entry varied in severity from the outer gate to the inner gates.

sentences.zh: 宜令宣徽院，籍兩省而下百官姓名，各依班序，聽通事舍人傳呼贊引，然後進。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the Palace Service to register the names of all officials from the two secretariats downward, each according to rank order, and let relay clerks call and lead them in before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Service should register every official from the two secretariats down, line them up by rank, and have relay clerks announce and escort them in turn.

sentences.zh: 其越次者，殿中司糾察定罰，不應入而入者，準闌入罪，庶朝廷之禮，漸可整肅。」

translations.literal: Those who overstep order should be investigated and penalized by the Hall Service; those who should not enter but do should be punished according to forcible-entry law—then court ritual may gradually be put in order."
translations.idiomatic: The Hall Service should punish anyone who breaks rank. Unauthorized entrants should be charged with forcible entry. Only then can court decorum be restored."

sentences.zh: 於是儀制始定。

translations.literal: Thereupon court ritual was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Court ceremony was established accordingly.

sentences.zh: 曲阜孔子廟，歷代給民百戶，以供洒掃，復其家，至是，尚書省以括戶之故，盡收為民，磐言：「林廟戶百家，歲賦鈔不過六百貫，僅比一六品官終年俸耳。

translations.literal: At the Confucius temple in Qufu, successive dynasties granted a hundred households for sweeping and sprinkling and exempted their families; at this time the Department of State Affairs, because of household registration consolidation, took them all back as common subjects. Pan said: "The forest-temple households number one hundred families; annual tax in paper money is no more than six hundred strings—merely equal to one sixth-rank official's yearly salary.
translations.idiomatic: At Confucius's temple in Qufu, past dynasties had granted a hundred households to maintain the grounds and exempted them from tax. Now the Department of State Affairs, during a household registration drive, reclassified them as ordinary subjects. Pan said, "The temple households number one hundred families. Their yearly tax in paper notes is barely six hundred strings—about one sixth-rank official's annual salary.

sentences.zh: 聖朝疆宇萬里，財賦歲億萬計，豈愛一六品官俸，不以待孔子哉。

translations.literal: The sage dynasty's territory spans ten thousand li, revenues yearly count in hundreds of millions—would it begrudge one sixth-rank salary and not wait upon Confucius?
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty rules ten thousand li and collects billions in revenue each year. Would the court begrudge a sixth-rank salary and refuse to honor Confucius?

sentences.zh: 且於府庫所益無多，其損國體甚大。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the gain to the treasury is not great, while the harm to national dignity is very large."
translations.idiomatic: The treasury would gain little, yet the damage to the state's dignity would be great."

sentences.zh: 時論韙之。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝以天下獄囚滋多，敕諸路自死罪以下，縱遣歸家，期秋八月，悉來京師聽決，囚如期至，帝惻然憐之，盡原其罪。

translations.literal: The emperor, because prisoners throughout the realm were growing numerous, ordered all circuits to release those below capital crime to return home, with a deadline in the eighth month of autumn to come to the capital for judgment; prisoners arrived on schedule, the emperor was moved with pity, and pardoned all their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Because prisons were overflowing, the emperor ordered circuits to release all prisoners below capital offense to go home, then return to the capital in the eighth month for final judgment. When they arrived on time, he was moved to pity and pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 他日，命詞臣作詔，戒喻天下，皆不稱旨意，磐獨以縱囚之意命辭，帝喜曰：「此朕所欲言而不能者，卿乃能為朕言之。」

translations.literal: Another day he ordered literary officials to compose an edict admonishing the realm; none matched his intent. Pan alone was commanded to phrase it on the meaning of releasing prisoners. The emperor rejoiced and said: "This is what I wished to say but could not—you were able to say it for me."
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor asked literary officials to draft an edict explaining the amnesty to the realm; none satisfied him. Pan alone was told to capture the spirit of the release. The emperor said with delight, "This is what I wanted to say but could not—you said it for me."

sentences.zh: 嘉獎不已，取酒賜之。

translations.literal: He praised him without end and took wine to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Pan repeatedly and gave him wine.

sentences.zh: 再乞致仕，不允。

translations.literal: He again requested retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to retire; again the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒許衡將告歸，帝遣近臣問磐，磐言：「衡素廉介，意其所以求退者，得非生員數少，坐縻廩祿，有所不安耶﹖宜增益生員，使之施教，則庶幾人材有成，衡之受祿亦可少安矣。」

translations.literal: Xu Heng, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, was about to request leave to return home; the emperor sent a close attendant to ask Pan. Pan said: "Heng has always been upright and incorruptible; I suspect his reason for seeking withdrawal may be that student numbers are few while he sits consuming salary grain and feels uneasy. Student numbers should be increased so he may teach—then talents may be formed, and Heng's receipt of salary may also be somewhat eased."
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Heng, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, planned to resign, the emperor asked Pan's view. Pan said, "Xu Heng is famously upright. Perhaps he feels uneasy drawing a salary while teaching so few students. Increase enrollment so he can teach properly—then students will flourish and his stipend will feel justified."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 磐移疾家居，帝遣使存問，賜以名藥。

translations.literal: Pan reported illness and dwelt at home; the emperor sent envoys to inquire after him and bestowed famous medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Pan took sick leave at home; the emperor sent envoys to inquire after his health and gifted him fine medicines.

sentences.zh: 磐嘗於會集議事之際，數言：「前代用人，二十從政，七十致仕，所以資其材力，閔其衰老，養其廉恥之心也。

translations.literal: Pan had often said at gatherings when deliberating affairs: "Former dynasties employed men at twenty for government and retired them at seventy—thereby supporting their talent and strength, pitying their aging, and nurturing their sense of integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: At council meetings Pan often said, "Earlier dynasties put men in office at twenty and retired them at seventy—to use their prime, spare their old age, and preserve their sense of honor.

sentences.zh: 今入仕者不限年，而老病者不能退，彼既不自知恥，朝廷亦不以為非，甚不可也。」

translations.literal: Today entrants to office are not limited by age, yet the old and ill cannot withdraw; they themselves no longer know shame, and the court also does not regard it as wrong—this is very unacceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Today there is no age limit for office, yet the old and sick cannot step down. They feel no shame, and the court sees nothing wrong with it. That cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 至是，以疾，請斷月俸毋給，自秋及春，堅乞致仕。

translations.literal: At this time, because of illness, he requested that monthly salary be cut off and not given; from autumn through spring he firmly begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Now, citing illness, he asked that his monthly salary be suspended. From autumn through spring he pressed hard for retirement.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使慰諭之曰：「卿年雖老，非任劇務，何以辭為。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to comfort and instruct him, saying: "Though your years are many, you are not assigned heavy duties—why resign?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to console him: "You are old, but you are not given heavy duties—why insist on leaving?"

sentences.zh: 仍詔祿之終身，併還所斷月俸。

translations.literal: He still ordered salary for life and also returned the suspended monthly payments.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered lifetime salary anyway and restored the payments Pan had refused.

sentences.zh: 磐不得已，復起。

translations.literal: Pan had no choice and returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: Pan had no choice but to return to service.

sentences.zh: 時方伐宋，凡帷幄謀議，有所未決，即遣使問之，磐所敷陳，每稱上意。

translations.literal: At the time they were campaigning against Song; whenever counsel in the command tent was undecided, envoys were sent to ask him, and what Pan presented always matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: While the Song campaign was underway, whenever strategy in council stalled, the emperor sent for Pan. Pan's advice always hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 帝將用兵日本，問以便宜，磐言：「今方伐宋，當用吾全力，庶可一舉取之。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to use troops against Japan and asked what was expedient. Pan said: "Now we are campaigning against Song—we should use our full strength so we may take it in one effort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned war against Japan and asked his view, Pan said, "We are already fighting the Song. Commit our full strength and we can take them in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 若復分力東夷，恐曠日持久，功卒難成。

translations.literal: If we again divide strength toward the eastern barbarians, I fear days will drag on long and achievement will ultimately be hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: If we split our forces toward the eastern islands, the war will drag on and success may slip away.

sentences.zh: 俟宋滅，徐圖之未晚也。」

translations.literal: Wait until Song is destroyed—planning it slowly will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the Song are gone; Japan can be dealt with later."

sentences.zh: 江南既下，磐上疏，大略言：「禁戢軍士，選擇官吏，賞功罰罪，推廣恩信，所以撫安新附，銷弭寇盜。」

translations.literal: After the south of the Yangzi was taken, Pan submitted a memorial roughly saying: "Restrain soldiers, select officials, reward merit and punish crime, extend grace and trust—these are means to pacify the newly submitted and eliminate bandits and robbers."
translations.idiomatic: After the south fell, Pan memorialized in essence: "Restrain the troops, choose good officials, reward merit and punish wrongdoing, and extend grace and trust—that is how to pacify new subjects and suppress banditry."

sentences.zh: 其言要切，皆見施行。

translations.literal: His words were essential and urgent; all were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: His points were sharp and practical, and all were adopted.

sentences.zh: 朝議汰冗官，權近私以按察司不便，欲併省之。

translations.literal: The court discussed eliminating redundant offices; powerful favorites privately said the surveillance commission was inconvenient and wished to merge and abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated cutting redundant offices. Powerful favorites privately complained that surveillance commissioners were inconvenient and wanted them abolished.

sentences.zh: 磐奏疏曰：「各路州郡，去京師遙遠，貪官污吏，侵害小民，無所控告，惟賴按察司為之申理。

translations.literal: Pan's memorial said: "Prefectures and districts of each circuit are far from the capital; greedy and corrupt officials harm common people with nowhere to appeal—they rely solely on the surveillance commission to present their cases.
translations.idiomatic: Pan wrote, "Prefectures lie far from the capital. Greedy officials prey on common people who have nowhere to appeal except through the surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 若指為冗官，一例罷去，則小民冤死而無所訴矣。

translations.literal: If they are labeled redundant offices and abolished wholesale, then common people will die wronged with nowhere to complain.
translations.idiomatic: If you call them redundant and abolish them, ordinary people will die with grievances and no recourse.

sentences.zh: 若曰京師有御史臺糾察四方之事，是大不然。

translations.literal: If one says the capital has the Censorate to investigate affairs in the four directions, that is greatly not so.
translations.idiomatic: To say the capital Censorate can oversee the whole realm is simply wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫御史臺，糾察朝廷百官、京畿州縣，尚有弗及，況能周遍外路千百城之事乎﹖若欲併入運司，運司專以營利增課為職，與管民官常分彼此，豈暇顧細民之冤抑哉﹖」由是按察司得不罷。

translations.literal: The Censorate investigates court officials and capital-area prefectures and counties—there are still matters it does not reach; how could it comprehensively cover affairs of outer circuits and thousands of cities? If one wishes to merge them into the Transport Office, the Transport Office specializes in seeking profit and increasing levies as its duty, often divided from civil officials who manage the people—how would it have leisure to attend to common people's wrongs and grievances?" Thereupon the surveillance commission was not abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate inspects court officials and the capital region and still misses cases—how could it cover thousands of towns in distant circuits? If you fold surveillance into the transport offices, whose job is profit and higher taxes and who already ignore the people, who will hear common grievances?" The surveillance commissioners were spared."

sentences.zh: 朝廷錄平宋功，遷至宰相執政者二十餘人，因議更定官制，磐奏疏曰：「歷代制度，有官品，有爵號，有職位，官爵所以示榮寵，職位所以委事權。

translations.literal: The court recorded merit in pacifying Song and promoted more than twenty men to chancellor and chief administrator; they therefore discussed revising the official system. Pan's memorial said: "Successive dynasties' institutions had office grades, noble titles, and posts—office and title show honor and favor; posts delegate administrative authority.
translations.idiomatic: After recording merit for conquering the Song, the court promoted more than twenty men to chancellor-level posts and debated reorganizing offices. Pan wrote, "Past dynasties distinguished rank, noble title, and actual post—rank and title honor a man; the post carries real authority.

sentences.zh: 臣下有功有勞，隨其大小，酬以官爵，有才有能，稱其所堪，處以職位，此人君御下之術也。

translations.literal: When subjects have merit and labor, according to its size reward with office and title; when they have talent and ability, match what they can bear and place them in posts—this is the ruler's art of governing subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Reward merit with rank and titles; place able men in posts they can handle—that is how a ruler governs.

sentences.zh: 臣以為有功者，宜加遷散官，或賜五等爵號，如漢、唐封侯之制可也，不宜任以職位。」

translations.literal: Your subject believes those with merit should receive promotion in honorary office or be granted five-rank noble titles, as Han and Tang enfeoffment of marquises may serve—they should not be assigned to governing posts."
translations.idiomatic: I believe men with merit should receive honorary promotions or five-rank noble titles, as in Han and Tang enfeoffment—not be given governing posts."

sentences.zh: 日本之役，師行有期，磐入諫曰：「日本小夷，海道險遠，勝之則不武，不勝則損威，臣以為勿伐便。」

translations.literal: For the campaign against Japan, when the army's departure had a set date, Pan entered to remonstrate: "Japan is a small barbarian land; the sea route is perilous and far. If victorious it is not martial glory; if not victorious it damages prestige—your subject believes not campaigning is expedient."
translations.idiomatic: As the Japan expedition was scheduled to sail, Pan remonstrated: "Japan is a petty island realm, the sea route long and dangerous. Victory brings little glory; defeat harms our prestige. Better not go."

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，謂非所宜言，且曰：「此在吾國法，言者不赦，汝豈有他心而然耶﹖」磐對曰：「臣赤心為國，故敢以言，苟有他心，何為從叛亂之地，冒萬死而來歸乎﹖今臣年已八十，況無子嗣，他心欲何為耶﹖」明日，帝遣侍臣以溫言慰撫，使無憂懼。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, saying it was not what should be spoken, and also said: "In our nation's law, speakers are not pardoned—do you have another heart in acting thus?" Pan replied: "Your subject has a loyal heart for the state and therefore dares speak. If I had another heart, why would I have come from rebellious territory, braving ten thousand deaths to return? Now your subject's years are already eighty, moreover without heirs—what other heart could I intend?" The next day the emperor sent attending officials with warm words to comfort him and put away fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and said such words were forbidden on pain of death: "Do you harbor ulterior motives?" Pan answered, "I speak from loyalty. If I had hidden aims, why would I have fled a rebel, risked death, and come to you? I am eighty and childless—what could I possibly plot?" The next day the emperor sent attendants with kind words to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 後閱內府珍玩，有碧玉寶枕，因出賜之。

translations.literal: Later, reviewing precious curios in the inner treasury, there was a jade-green treasure pillow, which he therefore took out and bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while reviewing treasures in the inner storehouse, the emperor found a jade pillow and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 磐以年老，累乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Pan, because of old age, repeatedly begged to return his bones.
translations.idiomatic: Growing old, Pan repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 丞相和禮霍孫為言，詔允其請，進資德大夫，致仕，仍給半俸終身。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Heli Huosun spoke on his behalf; an edict granted his request, promoted him to Grand Master of Virtuous Integrity, retired him, and still granted half salary for life.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Heli Huosun interceded; the emperor approved, promoted him to Grand Master of Virtuous Integrity, granted retirement, and paid half salary for life.

sentences.zh: 皇太子聞其去，召入宮，賜食，慰問良久。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince, hearing of his departure, summoned him into the palace, bestowed food, and consoled and inquired for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, hearing he was leaving, summoned him, gave a meal, and talked with him at length.

sentences.zh: 行之日，公卿百官，皆設宴以餞。

translations.literal: On the day of his departure, dukes, ministers, and all officials set banquets to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure day, ministers and officials held farewell banquets.

sentences.zh: 明日，皇太子賜宴聖安寺，公卿百官出送麗澤門外，縉紳以為榮。

translations.literal: The next day the Crown Prince gave a banquet at Sheng'an Temple; dukes, ministers, and all officials went out to send him off beyond Lizhe Gate—the gentry regarded it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the crown prince hosted a banquet at Sheng'an Temple; officials escorted him beyond Lizhe Gate—a signal honor for the gentry.

sentences.zh: 磐無子，命其壻著作郎李稚賓為東平判官，以便養。

translations.literal: Pan had no son; he ordered his son-in-law, Editing Gentleman Li Zhibin, to be Dongping Adjudicator for convenient support.
translations.idiomatic: Pan had no sons; he arranged for his son-in-law Li Zhibin, an editing gentleman, to serve as Dongping adjudicator so the family could care for him nearby.

sentences.zh: 每大臣燕見，帝數問磐起居狀，始終眷顧不衰。

translations.literal: Whenever great ministers attended banquets and audiences, the emperor repeatedly asked about Pan's daily condition; favor and care never declined.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ministers attended court, the emperor asked after Pan's health. His favor never waned.

sentences.zh: 磐資性剛方，閑居不妄言笑，每奏對，必以正，不肯阿意承順，帝嘗以古直稱之，雖權倖側目，弗顧也。

translations.literal: Pan's nature was stern and upright; in leisure he did not speak or laugh rashly; whenever he answered at audience he was always direct, unwilling to flatter and comply— the emperor once called him anciently straight; though powerful favorites glared sideways, he did not care.
translations.idiomatic: Pan was stern and upright. At home he seldom joked; in audience he spoke plainly and never flattered. The emperor called him "straight as the ancients." Powerful favorites glared, but he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬方得權，致重幣求文于碑，磐拒弗與，所薦宋、雷膺、魏初、徐琰、胡祗遹、孟祺、李謙，後皆為名臣。

translations.literal: When Ahmad had just gained power, he sent heavy gifts seeking an inscription for a stele; Pan refused and would not give it. Those he recommended—Song Qing, Lei Ying, Wei Chu, Xu Yan, Hu Zhiyuan, Meng Qi, and Li Qian—later all became famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Ahmad first rose to power, he offered rich gifts for a commemorative inscription; Pan refused. Those he recommended—Song Qing, Lei Ying, Wei Chu, Xu Yan, Hu Zhiyuan, Meng Qi, and Li Qian—all later became celebrated ministers.

sentences.zh: 年至九十二，卒之夕，有大星隕正寢之東。

translations.literal: His years reached ninety-two; on the night he died, a great star fell east of his main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He lived to ninety-two. On the night he died, a great star fell east of his bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 贈端貞雅亮佐治功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司，追封洺國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the merit title Upright, Loyal, Elegant, and Bright Assistant in Governance, Grand Tutor, and Grand Master with equal ceremony to the Three Excellencies; enfeoffed as Duke of Mo posthumously; temple name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Upright and Bright Assistant in Governance, Grand Tutor, and Grand Master of equal ceremony to the Three Excellencies; enfeoffed as Duke of Mo; given the posthumous name Wenzhong (Loyal and Cultured).

sentences.zh: 王鶚字百一，曹州東明人。

translations.literal: Wang E, style name Baiyi, was a man of Dongming in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, courtesy name Baiyi, was from Dongming in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖成，祖立，父琛。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Cheng, grandfather Li, father Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Li, and his father Chen.

sentences.zh: 鶚始生，有大鳥止於庭，鄉先生張奫曰：「鶚也。

translations.literal: When E was first born, a great bird stopped in the courtyard; the village elder Zhang Yu said: "It is an eagle.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth a large bird alighted in the courtyard. The local teacher Zhang Yu said, "An eagle.

sentences.zh: 是兒其有大名乎！」

translations.literal: This child will surely have a great name!"
translations.idiomatic: This child will win a great name!"

sentences.zh: 因名之。

translations.literal: Therefore he was named thus.
translations.idiomatic: So they named him E (Eagle).

sentences.zh: 幼聰悟，日誦千餘言，長工詞賦。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever and perceptive, reciting more than a thousand words a day; grown, he excelled at lyric and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick-witted and memorized more than a thousand characters a day; as an adult he excelled at poetry and fu.

sentences.zh: 甲辰冬，世祖在藩邸，訪求遺逸之士，遣使聘鶚。

translations.literal: In the winter of jiachen [1244], the Founder was at his princely residence seeking reclusive worthies and sent envoys to invite E.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 1244, while still a prince, Kublai sought hidden talent and sent envoys to invite Wang E.

sentences.zh: 及至，使者數輩迎勞，召對。

translations.literal: When he arrived, several envoys welcomed and comforted him, and he was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival several envoys welcomed him, and he was summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 進講孝經、書、易，及齊家治國之道，古今事物之變，每夜分，乃罷。

translations.literal: He lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, Documents, and Changes, and on ways to order the family and govern the state and changes of things ancient and modern; each session lasted until midnight before ending.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Documents, and the Changes, on household order and statecraft, and on historical change—sessions often ran until midnight.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「我雖未能即行汝言，安知異日不能行之耶！」

translations.literal: The Founder said: "Though I may not be able to carry out your words immediately, who knows whether in another day I cannot implement them!"
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "I may not act on your advice at once—but who knows whether I cannot do so someday?"

sentences.zh: 歲餘，乞還，賜以馬，仍命近侍闊闊、柴禎等五人從之學。

translations.literal: After more than a year he begged to return; he was given a horse, and five close attendants—Kuoku, Chai Zhen, and others—were ordered to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he asked to go home. The prince gave him a horse and ordered five close attendants, including Kuoku and Chai Zhen, to study under him.

sentences.zh: 繼命徙居大都，賜宅一所。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to move his residence to Dadu and was granted one house.
translations.idiomatic: He was later told to move to Dadu and given a house.

sentences.zh: 嘗因見，請曰：「天兵克蔡，金主自縊，其奉御絳山焚葬汝水之傍，禮為舊君有服，願往葬祭。」

translations.literal: Once on an audience he requested: "When the heavenly army took Cai, the Jin ruler hanged himself; his attendant Jiangshan burned and buried him beside the Ru River. By ritual one wears mourning for a former lord—I wish to go bury and sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: On one audience he asked, "When our army took Cai, the Jin emperor hanged himself. His attendant Jiangshan burned and buried him by the Ru River. By ritual I owe mourning to a former sovereign—I wish to go and perform the rites."

sentences.zh: 世祖義而許之，至則為河水所沒，設具牲酒，為位而哭。

translations.literal: The Founder approved it as righteous and permitted it. When he arrived, the site had been submerged by river water; he set out sacrificial animals and wine and made a place to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai approved the request as righteous. When Wang E arrived, the grave had been washed away by the river; he set out offerings and wept at a memorial place.

sentences.zh: 有言事者，謂宰執非其人，詔儒臣廷議可任宰相者。

translations.literal: There were memorialists who said the chief ministers were not the right men; an edict ordered Confucian officials to debate in court who could serve as grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials memorialized that the chief ministers were unfit for their posts, and the emperor ordered Confucian court scholars to debate who might serve as grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬巧佞，欲乘隙取相位，大臣復助之，衆知其非，莫敢言。

translations.literal: At the time Ahmad was artful and fawning; he wished to seize an opening to take the position of chief minister, and great ministers again assisted him; the multitude knew it was wrong but none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad was cunning and obsequious and sought to exploit the moment to win the chancellorship, with senior ministers backing him; everyone knew it was wrong, but no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 鶚奮然擲筆曰：「吾以衰老之年，無以報國，即欲舉任此人為相，吾不能插驢尾矣。」

translations.literal: E, stirred, cast down his brush and said: "With my aged and declining years I have no means to repay the state; even if you wish to nominate and appoint this man as chief minister, I cannot insert myself in a donkey's tail."
translations.idiomatic: Wang E flung down his brush and declared, "In my old age I have little left with which to serve the state—but if you mean to make this man chancellor, I refuse to tuck myself into a donkey's tail."

sentences.zh: 振袖而起，奸計為之中止。

translations.literal: He shook his sleeves and rose; the treacherous plot was thereby halted midway.
translations.idiomatic: He swept his sleeves and walked out, and the scheme was stopped cold.

sentences.zh: 五年，乞致仕，詔有司歲給廩祿終其身，有大事則遣使就問之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he begged to retire from office; an edict ordered the relevant offices to grant him grain stipend annually for life, and when great matters arose envoys would be sent to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1268) he asked to retire. The court ordered that his salary be paid for life and that envoys consult him whenever major affairs arose.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，年八十四，諡文康。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died, age eighty-four; posthumous name Wenkang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year (1273), aged eighty-four, and was given the posthumous name Wenkang (Cultured and Vigorous).

sentences.zh: 鶚性樂易，為文章不事雕飾，嘗曰：「學者當以窮理為先，分章析句，乃經生舉子之業，非為己之學也。」

translations.literal: E by nature was easygoing and cheerful; in composing writing he did not pursue ornamentation. He once said: "Scholars ought to take penetrating principle first; dividing chapters and analyzing sentences are merely the tasks of Classicist examination candidates—not learning for oneself."
translations.idiomatic: Wang E was good-natured and wrote without ornamental fuss. He once said, "A scholar should seek to grasp underlying principles first; parsing chapters and clauses is work for exam candidates, not true self-cultivation."

sentences.zh: 著論語集義一卷，汝南遺事二卷，詩文四十卷，曰應物集。

translations.literal: He authored one juan of Collected Meanings of the Analects, two juan of Remnant Affairs of Runan, and forty juan of poetry and prose called the Collection in Response to Things.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collected Meanings of the Analects (1 juan), Remnant Affairs of Runan (2 juan), and forty juan of poetry and prose entitled Collection in Response to Things.

sentences.zh: 無子，以壻周鐸子之綱承其祀。

translations.literal: He had no son; he made Zhigang, son of his son-in-law Zhou Duo, continue his sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, he adopted Zhigang, son of his son-in-law Zhou Duo, to carry on the family line.

sentences.zh: 之綱，官至翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: Zhigang rose to Attendant Lecturer in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigang later served as Hanlin Attendant Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 高鳴字雄飛，真定人，少以文學知名。

translations.literal: Gao Ming, style name Xiongfei, was a man of Zhending; in youth he was renowned for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ming, courtesy name Xiongfei, was from Zhending and won early fame for his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 河東元裕上書薦之，不報。

translations.literal: Yuan Yu of Hedong submitted a memorial recommending him; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yu of Hedong recommended him in a memorial, but the court took no action.

sentences.zh: 諸王旭烈兀將征西域，聞其賢，遣使者三輩召之，鳴乃起，為王陳西征二十餘策，王數稱善，即薦為彰德路緫管。

translations.literal: When Prince Hulagu was about to campaign in the Western Regions, hearing of his worth he sent three successive envoys to summon him; Ming then rose, presented more than twenty strategies for the western expedition to the prince, the prince repeatedly praised them as good, and immediately recommended him as Commissioner of Zhangde Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hulagu prepared to march west, he heard of Gao Ming's reputation and sent three envoys to fetch him. Gao Ming responded, laid out more than twenty plans for the campaign, and earned repeated praise; the prince then recommended him as commissioner of Zhangde Circuit.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，賜誥命金符，已而召為翰林學士，兼太常少卿。

translations.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, he was granted patent and golden tally; shortly thereafter he was summoned as Hanlin Academician, concurrently Vice Minister of the Grand Impartial.
translations.idiomatic: After Kublai took the throne, Gao Ming received an appointment patent and gold tally, then was summoned as Hanlin Academician and concurrent Vice Minister of the Grand Impartial.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，立御史臺，以鳴為侍御史，風紀條章，多其裁定。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan the Censorate was established; Ming was made Attendant Censor, and many provisions of disciplinary regulations were determined by him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1268 the Censorate was established and Gao Ming appointed Attendant Censor; he drafted much of its disciplinary code.

sentences.zh: 尋立四道按察司，選任名士，鳴所薦居多，時論咸稱其知人。

translations.literal: Soon four regional surveillance commissions were established; eminent scholars were selected and appointed, and those Ming recommended were the majority; contemporary opinion unanimously praised his knowledge of men.
translations.idiomatic: When four regional surveillance commissions were soon established, Gao Ming's recommendations supplied most of the appointees, and contemporaries praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 天下初定，中書、樞密事多壅滯，言者請置督事官各二人，鳴曰：「官得人，自無滯政，臣職在奉憲，願舉察之，毋為員外置人也。」

translations.literal: When the realm was first pacified, affairs of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs were often blocked and delayed; memorialists requested establishing two overseers of affairs each; Ming said: "If offices get the right men, there will naturally be no obstructed governance; my duty lies in upholding the statutes—I wish to investigate and censure; do not establish extra posts outside the regular establishment."
translations.idiomatic: With the realm newly pacified, Secretariat and Military Affairs business often stalled. Some proposed adding two overseers for each. Gao Ming replied, "Pick the right officials and work will not pile up. My job is to enforce the law through investigation—do not create positions outside the regular establishment."

sentences.zh: 七年，議立三省，鳴上封事曰：「臣聞三省，設自近古，其法由中書出政，移門下，議不合，則有駁正，或封還詔書；

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when establishing the Three Departments was debated, Ming submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the Three Departments were set up from recent antiquity; their method was that the Secretariat issued policy, forwarded it to the Chancellery; if deliberation did not agree, there was refutation and correction, or the edict might be sealed and returned;
translations.idiomatic: In 1270, when the Three Departments system was proposed, Gao Ming submitted a sealed memorial: "The Three Departments date from antiquity. Policy issued from the Secretariat went to the Chancellery; if they disagreed, the Chancellery could refute it or seal and return the edict;

sentences.zh: 議合，則還移中書；

translations.literal: if deliberation agreed, it was returned and forwarded to the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: if they agreed, it went back to the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 中書移尚書，尚書乃下六部、郡國。

translations.literal: the Secretariat forwarded to the Department of State Affairs, and the Department of State Affairs then promulgated down to the Six Ministries and commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: the Secretariat forwarded it to the Department of State Affairs, which then sent it to the Six Ministries and the provinces.

sentences.zh: 方今天下大於古，而事益繁，取決一省，猶曰有壅，況三省乎！

translations.literal: Now the realm under Heaven is larger than in antiquity and affairs are ever more numerous; deciding through one department is still said to have obstruction—how much more three departments!
translations.idiomatic: Today's empire is larger than antiquity and business grows ever heavier. Even a single department is accused of causing bottlenecks—how much worse would three be!

sentences.zh: 且多置官者，求免失政也，但使賢俊萃于一堂，連署參決，自免失政，豈必別官異坐，而後無失政乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, increasing offices seeks to avoid failed governance; but if worthy and eminent men gather in one hall and jointly sign deliberating decisions, they will naturally avoid failed governance—must one necessarily have separate officials in separate seats before there will be no failed governance!
translations.idiomatic: Extra posts are meant to prevent bad government—but if capable men sit together and decide jointly, they can avoid failure without separate offices and separate seats!

sentences.zh: 故曰：政貴得人，不貴多官。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: governance values getting the right men, not valuing many officials.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, good government depends on the right people, not on multiplying offices.

sentences.zh: 不如一省便。」

translations.literal: It is better that one department is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: A single department would be simpler."

sentences.zh: 世祖深然之，議遂罷。

translations.literal: The Founder deeply agreed with this; the proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai strongly agreed, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 川、陝盜起，省臣患之，請專戮其尤者以止盜，朝議將從之，鳴諫曰：「制令天下上死囚，必待論報，所以重用刑、惜民生也。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Chuan and Shanxi; provincial ministers were troubled and requested summary execution of the worst to stop banditry; court deliberation was about to accede; Ming remonstrated: "Regulations command that throughout the realm when submitting death-sentence prisoners, one must await review and report—that is why heavy use of punishment is restrained and people's lives are cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry broke out in Sichuan and Shaanxi. Provincial officials, alarmed, asked to execute ringleaders summarily. The court was inclined to agree until Gao Ming objected: "The law requires that all capital cases be reported and reviewed before execution—that is how the state restrains harsh punishment and protects the people.

sentences.zh: 今從其請，是開天下擅殺之路，害仁政甚大。」

translations.literal: Now if their request is followed, this opens the road throughout the realm to unauthorized killing—greatly harming benevolent governance."
translations.idiomatic: Granting this request would open the door to unauthorized killings everywhere and do grave harm to humane rule."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰「善」，令速止之。

translations.literal: The Founder said "Good" and ordered it quickly stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said "Well said" and ordered the proposal halted at once.

sentences.zh: 鳴每以敢言被上知，嘗入內，值大風雪，帝謂御史大夫塔察兒曰：「高學士年老，後有大政，就問可也。」

translations.literal: Ming was often known to the sovereign for daring speech; once he entered the palace during a great wind and snowstorm; the Emperor said to Censor-in-Chief Tacar: "Academician Gao is aged; when great governance arises later, you may consult him."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ming won the emperor's trust through blunt counsel. Once, entering the palace in a blizzard, the emperor told Censor-in-Chief Tacar, "Academician Gao is old; on major questions you may go and ask him."

sentences.zh: 賜太官酒肉慰勞之，其見敬禮如此。

translations.literal: He was granted palace wine and meat to comfort and reward him; such was the respect and courtesy shown him.
translations.idiomatic: He was given palace wine and meat as a reward—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷吏禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of the Personnel and Rites Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1272 he was appointed Minister of the Personnel and Rites Ministries.

sentences.zh: 十一年，病卒，年六十六，有文集五十卷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died of illness, age sixty-six; he had a collected works of fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in 1274, aged sixty-six, leaving a fifty-juan collected works.

sentences.zh: 李冶字仁卿，真定欒城人。

translations.literal: Li Ye, style name Renqing, was a man of Luancheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye, courtesy name Renqing, was from Luancheng in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 登金進士第，調高陵簿，未上，辟知鈞州事。

translations.literal: He passed the Jin advanced scholar examination; was assigned as Clerk of Gaoling, did not take up the post, and was invited to serve as Prefect of Jun prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Jin jinshi examination and was assigned clerk of Gaoling, but before reporting he was invited to govern Jun prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲壬辰，城潰，冶微服北渡，流落忻、崞間，聚書環堵，人所不堪，冶處之裕如也。

translations.literal: In the year renchen the city walls collapsed; Ye in plain dress crossed north; he drifted between Xin and Guo, gathered books filling his walls; what others could not endure, Ye dwelt in with ample ease.
translations.idiomatic: In 1232, when the city walls gave way, Li Ye slipped north in plain clothes and wandered between Xin and Guo. He piled books wall to wall in quarters others found unbearable, yet lived there at ease.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸，聞其賢，遣使召之，且曰：「素聞仁卿學優才贍，潛德不耀，久欲一見，其勿他辭。」

translations.literal: When the Founder was at the princely residence, hearing of his worth he sent an envoy to summon him, saying: "I have long heard Renqing's learning is superior and talents abundant, hidden virtue not displayed—I have long wished to meet once; do not decline for other reasons."
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince, Kublai heard of Li Ye's reputation and sent envoys to summon him, saying, "I have long heard that Renqing's learning is deep and his talent broad, his virtue modest and unsung. I have wanted to meet you for some time—please do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 既至，問河南居官者孰賢，對曰：「險夷一節，惟完顏仲德。」

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was asked which officials serving in Henan were worthy; he replied: "Steadfast through peril and ease—only Wanyan Zhongde."
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, Kublai asked which Henan officials were worthy. Li Ye answered, "For constancy in adversity and comfort, only Wanyan Zhongde."

sentences.zh: 又問完顏合荅及蒲瓦何如，對曰：「二人將略短少，任之不疑，此金所以亡也。」

translations.literal: He was again asked what of Wanyan Heda and Puwa; he replied: "These two men's generalship was shallow and deficient; appointing them without doubt—this is why Jin perished."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Wanyan Heda and Puwa, he said, "Both were limited commanders, yet entrusted without question—that is one reason the Jin fell."

sentences.zh: 又問魏徵、曹彬何如，對曰：「徵忠言讜論，知無不言，以唐諍臣觀之，徵為第一。

translations.literal: He again asked what of Wei Zheng and Cao Bin; he replied: "Wei Zheng's loyal words and straightforward discourse—knowing nothing he did not speak—viewed among Tang's remonstrating ministers, Wei Zheng ranks first.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Wei Zheng and Cao Bin, he replied, "Wei Zheng spoke loyalty and plain truth and withheld nothing; among Tang's remonstrating ministers he ranks first.

sentences.zh: 彬伐江南，未嘗妄殺一人，儗之方叔、召虎可也。

translations.literal: Cao Bin in campaigning against Jiangnan never killed a person recklessly; one may compare him to Fang Shu and Zhao Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of the south Cao Bin never killed wantonly; he may be likened to Fang Shu and Zhao Hu of old.

sentences.zh: 漢之韓、彭、衛、霍，在所不論。」

translations.literal: Han's Han Xin, Peng Yue, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing need not be discussed."
translations.idiomatic: As for Han Xin, Peng Yue, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing of Han—not worth mentioning here."

sentences.zh: 又問今之臣有如魏徵者乎，對曰：「今以側媚成風，欲求魏征之賢，實難其人。」

translations.literal: He again asked whether among present ministers there were any like Wei Zheng; he replied: "Now with obsequious flattery forming the prevailing wind, to seek Wei Zheng's worthiness—truly it is hard to find such a person."
translations.idiomatic: Asked whether any minister today matched Wei Zheng, he said, "Flattery is now the fashion; to find another Wei Zheng would be very hard."

sentences.zh: 又問今之人材賢否，對曰：「天下未嘗乏材，求則得之，舍則失之，理勢然耳。

translations.literal: He again asked whether present talent was worthy or not; he replied: "The realm under Heaven has never lacked talent—seek and you obtain it, abandon and you lose it; such is the logic of circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: Asked whether talent was abundant today, he said, "The realm has never lacked capable men; seek them and they appear, neglect them and they vanish—that is simply how things work.

sentences.zh: 今儒生有如魏璠、王鶚、李獻卿、蘭光庭、趙復、郝經、王博文輩，皆有用之材，又皆賢王所嘗聘問者，舉而用之，何所不可，但恐用之不盡耳。

translations.literal: Now Confucian scholars such as Wei Fan, Wang E, Li Xianqing, Lan Guangting, Zhao Fu, Hao Jing, and Wang Bowen are all talent useful for employment, and all were men the worthy Prince once invited and questioned; raise them and employ them—what could not be done? Only fear they would not be fully used.
translations.idiomatic: Among Confucian scholars today, men like Wei Fan, Wang E, Li Xianqing, Lan Guangting, Zhao Fu, Hao Jing, and Wang Bowen are all useful talent—the very men Your Highness has already consulted. Employ them and nothing is impossible; the only risk is not using them fully.

sentences.zh: 然四海之廣，豈止此數子哉。

translations.literal: Yet with the four seas so vast, how could there be only these few men!
translations.idiomatic: Yet across the four seas, are there only these few?

sentences.zh: 王誠能旁求於外，將見集於明廷矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness truly can seek widely beyond, you will see them gather at the bright court."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness truly seeks widely abroad, they will gather at your enlightened court."

sentences.zh: 又問天下當何以治之，對曰：「夫治天下，難則難於登天，易則易於反掌。

translations.literal: He was again asked how to govern the realm; he replied: "Governing the realm under Heaven—hard, then it is harder than ascending Heaven; easy, then it is easier than turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Asked how to govern the realm, he replied, "Governing the empire can be harder than climbing to Heaven—or easier than turning one's hand.

sentences.zh: 蓋有法度則治，控名責實則治，進君子退小人則治，如是而治天下，豈不易於反掌乎。

translations.literal: For where there are laws and standards there is order; where names are controlled and reality is demanded there is order; where gentlemen are advanced and petty men are retired there is order—govern the realm under Heaven thus, is it not easier than turning the palm?
translations.idiomatic: With laws and standards there is order; with names matched to reality there is order; with gentlemen promoted and petty men dismissed there is order. Govern that way and is it not as easy as turning one's hand?

sentences.zh: 無法度則亂，有名無實則亂，進小人退君子則亂，如是而治天下，豈不難於登天乎。

translations.literal: Without laws and standards there is disorder; where there are names without reality there is disorder; where petty men are advanced and gentlemen are retired there is disorder—govern the realm under Heaven thus, is it not harder than ascending Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Without laws there is chaos; with empty titles and no substance there is chaos; with petty men promoted and gentlemen pushed aside there is chaos. Govern that way and is it not harder than climbing to Heaven?

sentences.zh: 且為治之道，不過立法度、正紀綱而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, the way of governance is nothing more than establishing laws and standards and rectifying discipline and norms.
translations.idiomatic: The art of governance comes down to establishing laws and restoring proper discipline.

sentences.zh: 紀綱者，上下相維持；

translations.literal: Discipline and norms are what above and below mutually uphold;
translations.idiomatic: Discipline is what binds ruler and subjects together;

sentences.zh: 法度者，賞罰示懲勸。

translations.literal: laws and standards are reward and punishment showing censure and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: laws are reward and punishment made visible as warning and incentive.

sentences.zh: 今則大官小吏，下至編氓，皆自縱恣，以私害公，是無法度也。

translations.literal: Now great officials and petty clerks, down to registered commoners, all indulge themselves freely, harming the public with private interest—this is having no laws and standards.
translations.idiomatic: Today great officials and petty clerks, down to the common people, indulge themselves and sacrifice the public good to private interest—that is lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 有功者未必得賞，有罪者未必被罰，甚則有功者或反受辱，有罪者或反獲寵，是無法度也。

translations.literal: Those with merit do not necessarily receive reward; those with guilt do not necessarily suffer punishment; in extreme cases those with merit may instead receive insult, those with guilt may instead obtain favor—this is having no laws and standards.
translations.idiomatic: Merit may go unrewarded and guilt unpunished; sometimes the meritorious are shamed while the guilty are favored—that too is lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 法度廢，紀綱壞，天下不變亂，已為幸矣。」

translations.literal: Laws and standards abandoned, discipline and norms ruined—if the realm under Heaven does not turn to disorder, that is already fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: With laws abandoned and discipline broken, it would be fortunate if the realm did not fall into chaos."

sentences.zh: 又問昨地震何如，對曰：「天裂為陽不足，地震為陰有餘。

translations.literal: He was again asked about yesterday's earthquake; he replied: "Heaven splitting signifies yang insufficiency; earthquake signifies yin surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the recent earthquake, he replied, "Heaven splitting means yang is insufficient; an earthquake means yin is excessive.

sentences.zh: 夫地道，陰也，陰太盛，則變常，今之地震，或姦邪在側，或女謁盛行，或讒慝交至，或刑罰失中，或征伐驟舉，五者必有一于此矣。

translations.literal: The way of earth is yin; when yin is too abundant, the normal changes. Today's earthquake—perhaps treacherous evil at one's side, or women's access flourishing, or slander and malice arriving together, or punishments missing the mean, or campaigns suddenly raised—of these five there must be one present.
translations.idiomatic: Earth is yin; when yin overwhelms, the natural order shifts. This earthquake may signal treacherous advisers at your side, undue influence of women at court, slander running rampant, punishments out of balance, or sudden military campaigns—one of these five must be at work.

sentences.zh: 夫天之愛君，如愛其子，故示此以警之耳。

translations.literal: Heaven's love for the sovereign is like love for its child; therefore it shows this to warn him.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven loves the sovereign as a father loves a son, and shows this sign to warn him.

sentences.zh: 苟能辨姦邪，去女謁，屏讒慝，省刑罰，慎征討，上當天心，下協人意，則可轉咎為休矣。」

translations.literal: If one can distinguish treacherous evil, remove women's access, screen out slander and malice, reduce punishments, and be cautious in campaigns and punitive expeditions—above matching Heaven's heart, below harmonizing people's intent—then one can turn calamity into blessing."
translations.idiomatic: If you can root out treachery, curb undue female influence, silence slander, lighten punishments, and wage war with caution—aligning with Heaven above and the people below—you may turn misfortune into blessing."

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Founder praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai praised the advice and took it to heart.

sentences.zh: 冶晚家元氏，買田封龍山下，學徒益衆。

translations.literal: In his later years Ye made his home at Yuanshi, bought fields below Mount Fenglong; his students daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: In old age Li Ye settled at Yuanshi, bought land below Mount Fenglong, and his students grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 及世祖即位，復聘之，欲處以清要，冶以老病，懇求還山。

translations.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, he again invited him; wishing to place him in a pure and important post, Ye cited old age and illness and earnestly begged to return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: After Kublai took the throne he invited Li Ye again and wished to give him a prestigious post, but Li Ye pleaded old age and illness and asked to return to his mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，再以學士召，就職期月，復以老病辭去，卒于家，年八十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan he was again summoned as Academician; he took office for one month, again declined on grounds of old age and illness, and died at home, age eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In 1265 he was summoned again as Hanlin Academician, served one month, resigned again citing old age and illness, and died at home aged eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 所著有敬齋文集四十卷，壁書藂削十二卷，泛說四十卷，古今黈四十卷，測圓海鏡十二卷，益古衍段三十卷。

translations.literal: His authored works include forty juan of Jingzhai Collected Writings, twelve juan of Brush Writings from the Wall, forty juan of General Discourses, forty juan of Ancient and Modern Yellow, twelve juan of Sea Mirror of Circular Surveying, and thirty juan of Ancient Supplementary Segments.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Jingzhai Collected Writings (40 juan), Brush Writings from the Wall (12 juan), General Discourses (40 juan), Ancient and Modern Yellow (40 juan), Sea Mirror of Circular Surveying (12 juan), and Ancient Supplementary Segments (30 juan).

sentences.zh: 李昶字士都，東平須城人。

translations.literal: Li Chang, style name Shidu, was a man of Xucheng in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang, courtesy name Shidu, was from Xucheng in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 父世弼，從外家受孫明復春秋，得其宗旨。

translations.literal: His father Shibi studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Sun Mingfu through his mother's family and obtained its essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shibi learned the Spring and Autumn Annals from Sun Mingfu through his mother's family and mastered its core principles.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐初，三赴廷試，不第，推恩授彭城簿，志壹鬱不樂，遂復求試。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jinyou era of Jin, he thrice attended the palace examination and did not pass; by grace he was appointed Clerk of Pengcheng, but his ambition was depressed and unhappy, so he again sought to take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jinyou era he took the palace examination three times without success and was granted the post of clerk of Pengcheng by grace, but he remained unhappy and sought to try again.

sentences.zh: 一夕，夢在李彥牓下及第，閱計偕之士，無之，時昶年十六，已能為程文，乃更其名曰彥。

translations.literal: One night he dreamed of passing the examination under Li Yan's placard; reviewing the candidates traveling together for the exam, there was none such; at the time Chang was sixteen and could already compose examination essays, so he changed his name to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed he had passed the exam under Li Yan's name on the roster; he checked the candidates and found no such person. Chang was sixteen and already skilled at exam essays, so he changed his name to Yan.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，父子廷試，昶果以春秋中第二甲第二人，世弼第三甲第三人，父子褒貶各異，時人以比向、歆，而世弼遂不復仕，晚乃授東平教授以卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding, father and son took the palace examination; Chang indeed passed on the Spring and Autumn Annals as second in the second rank, Shibi as third in the third rank; father and son received praise and censure each differently; contemporaries compared them to Xiang and Xin; Shibi then never again served in office, and only late in life was appointed Professor of Dongping until death.
translations.idiomatic: In 1222 father and son sat the palace exam together: Chang placed second in the second rank on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Shibi third in the third rank. Their fortunes diverged, and people compared them to Xiang Kuang and his son Xin. Shibi never served again and late in life became professor at Dongping, where he died.

sentences.zh: 昶穎悟過人，讀書如夙習，無故不出戶外，鄰里罕識其面。

translations.literal: Chang was quick-witted beyond others; reading was as if long practiced; without cause he did not go outside his door; neighbors rarely knew his face.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang was exceptionally quick-witted and read as if he had always known the texts. He rarely left home without reason, and neighbors scarcely knew him by sight.

sentences.zh: 初從父入科場，儕輩少之，譏議紛紜，監試者遠其次舍，伺察甚嚴。

translations.literal: When he first followed his father into the examination hall, his peers looked down on him and criticism was clamorous; the examination supervisors kept far from their lodging and watched very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the exam hall with his father, fellow candidates looked down on him and gossip spread; supervisors kept their distance but watched them closely.

sentences.zh: 昶肆筆數千言，比午，已脫稿。

translations.literal: Chang freely wrote several thousand words; by noon he had already finished his draft.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang wrote several thousand characters at a stroke and had finished his draft by noon.

sentences.zh: 釋褐，授徵事郎、孟州溫縣丞。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office dress he was appointed Gentleman of Promoting Affairs and Assistant Magistrate of Wen county in Meng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Upon passing the exam he was appointed Gentleman of Promoting Affairs and assistant magistrate of Wen county in Meng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 正大改元，超授儒林郎、賜緋魚袋、鄭州河陰簿。

translations.literal: At the inaugural year of Zhengda he was specially promoted to Gentleman of the Forest of Scholars, granted the crimson fish tally, and appointed Clerk of Heyin in Zheng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengda era he was promoted to Gentleman of the Forest of Scholars, given the crimson fish tally, and appointed clerk of Heyin in Zheng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，召試尚書省掾，再調漕運提舉。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned for examination as Secretariat clerk; he was again transferred to Commissioner of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was tested for a Secretariat clerkship and later transferred to commissioner of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 國兵下河南，奉親還鄉里。

translations.literal: When the state army descended on Henan, he escorted his parents and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mongol army entered Henan, he took his parents home.

sentences.zh: 行臺嚴實，辟授都事，改行軍萬戶府知事。

translations.literal: Yan Shi of the Branch Secretariat invited and appointed him Director; he was changed to Administrator of the Field Army Ten-Thousand-Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi of the Branch Secretariat recruited him as director and later made him administrator of the field army ten-thousand-households office.

sentences.zh: 實卒，子忠濟嗣，陞昶為經歷。

translations.literal: When Shi died, his son Zhongji succeeded; Chang was promoted to Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Shi died his son Zhongji succeeded him and promoted Li Chang to administrator.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，忠濟怠於政事，貪佞抵隙而進。

translations.literal: After several years Zhongji was slack in governance; the greedy and fawning pressed in through openings.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Zhongji grew negligent in affairs, and greedy flatterers seized their chance to advance.

sentences.zh: 昶言於忠濟曰：「比年內外裘馬相尚，飲宴無度，庫藏空虛，百姓匱乏，若猶循習故常，恐或生變。

translations.literal: Chang spoke to Zhongji, saying: "In recent years within and without, fur coats and horses are mutually admired; feasting without limit; treasury stores empty; the people impoverished—if one still follows old habits, I fear change may arise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang told Zhongji, "In recent years officials inside and out have competed in fine furs and horses and feasted without limit. The treasury is empty and the people are destitute. If you go on as before, trouble may follow.

sentences.zh: 惟閤下接納正士，黜遠小人，去浮華，敦樸素，損騎從，省宴游，雖不能救已然之失，尚可以弭未然之禍。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Lordship welcomes upright gentlemen, dismisses and keeps petty men at a distance, removes ostentation, promotes plain simplicity, reduces mounted attendants, and economizes on banquets and outings—though one cannot remedy faults already done, one may still quell calamities not yet come."
translations.idiomatic: If you welcome upright men, keep petty men at a distance, reject ostentation for plain living, cut your retinue, and curtail feasting and pleasure outings, you may not undo past mistakes but you can still avert future disaster."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷裁抑諸侯，法制寢密，忠濟縱侈自若，昶以親老求解，不許。

translations.literal: At the time the court was restraining feudal lords and laws and institutions grew ever tighter; Zhongji indulged in extravagance as before; Chang requested release on grounds of aged parents and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then curbing the princes and tightening the law, yet Zhongji lived as lavishly as ever. Li Chang asked to resign to care for his aged parents but was refused.

sentences.zh: 俄以父憂去官，杜門教授，一時名士，若李謙、馬紹、吳衍輩，皆出其門。

translations.literal: Soon on his father's bereavement he left office, closed his doors and taught; eminent men of the time such as Li Qian, Ma Shao, and Wu Yan all came from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he left office to mourn his father, he shut his doors and taught; leading scholars of the day, including Li Qian, Ma Shao, and Wu Yan, were among his pupils.

sentences.zh: 時徵需煩重，行中書省科徵稅賦，雖逋戶不貸，昶移書時相，其略曰：「百姓困於弊政久矣，聖上龍飛，首頒明詔，天下之人，如獲更生，拭目傾耳，以徯太平，半年之間，人漸失望，良以渴仰之心太切，興除之政未孚故也。

translations.literal: At the time requisitions were heavy and burdensome; the Branch Secretariat assessed and levied taxes and dues, not exempting even delinquent households; Chang sent a letter to the chief minister, its gist saying: "The people have long been trapped by corrupt governance; when the sage sovereign ascended like a dragon, he first issued a bright edict; people throughout the realm were as if reborn; they wiped their eyes and inclined their ears, awaiting great peace—in half a year people gradually lost hope, truly because the heart's thirst was too keen and policies of abolishing and establishing had not yet won trust.
translations.idiomatic: Tax levies were then heavy, and the Branch Secretariat collected dues even from delinquent households without relief. Li Chang wrote to the chief minister, in essence: "The people have long suffered under bad government. When the emperor took the throne he issued enlightened edicts, and the realm felt reborn—everyone watched and listened for peace. Within half a year hope faded, because expectations ran too high and reform had not yet taken hold.

sentences.zh: 側聞欲據丁巳戶籍，科徵租稅，比之見戶，或加多十六七，止驗見戶，應輸猶恐不逮，復令包補逃故，必致艱難。

translations.literal: I have heard on the side that you wish to base assessment on the dingsi household register to levy land tax and dues; compared with present households, it may increase by sixteen or seventeen tenths; even assessing only present households, what should be paid still fears falling short—again ordering bundled supplementation of fugitives and the deceased must lead to hardship.
translations.idiomatic: I hear you plan to levy taxes from the dingsi household register, which may increase the burden by as much as sixteen or seventeen parts in ten over current households. Even taxing only registered households may exceed what they can pay; forcing them to cover fugitives and the dead will only make matters worse.

sentences.zh: 苟不以撫字安集為心，惟事供億，則諸人皆能之，豈聖上擢賢更化之意哉﹖」於是省府為蠲逋戶之賦。

translations.literal: If one does not take comforting and settling the people as one's heart but only serves supply and tribute, then anyone can do that—how is this the sage sovereign's intent in elevating the worthy and changing governance?" Thereupon the province and prefecture remitted taxes for delinquent households."
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is not to settle and care for the people but merely to meet quotas, anyone can do that—is that what the emperor meant by elevating the worthy and reforming government?" The provincial offices then remitted taxes for delinquent households."

sentences.zh: 中統二年春，內難平，昶上表賀，因進諷諫曰：「患難所以存儆戒，禍亂將以開聖明，伏願日新其德，雖休勿休，戰勝不矜，功成不有，和輯宗親，撫綏將士，增修庶政，選用百官，儉以足用，寬以養民，安不忘危，治不忘亂，恒以北征宵旰之勤，永為南面逸豫之戒。」

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Zhongtong, when internal troubles were pacified, Chang submitted a congratulatory memorial and therein offered admonitory counsel, saying: "Adversity exists to preserve warning and caution; calamity and disorder will open the way to sage clarity. I humbly wish daily renewal of virtue; though at rest, do not rest; though victorious in battle, do not boast; though merit is achieved, do not claim possession; harmonize and gather kin; comfort and pacify generals and soldiers; increase and repair various governance; select and employ the hundred officials; be frugal to suffice in use, be lenient to nourish the people; in security do not forget peril, in order do not forget disorder; always take the northern campaign's toil till midnight as model, forever make it a warning against southern-facing ease and pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1261, after internal strife was settled, Li Chang submitted a congratulatory memorial with admonition: "Hardship preserves warning; turmoil can awaken wisdom. I pray Your Majesty renew your virtue daily—rest, but do not slacken; win battles, but do not boast; achieve success, but do not claim it for yourself. Reconcile your kin, comfort your officers and soldiers, improve governance, and choose worthy officials. Be frugal yet sufficient, lenient yet nourishing. In peace remember danger; in order remember chaos. Let the sleepless toil of the northern campaigns forever warn against the ease of ruling from the south in comfort."

sentences.zh: 世祖稱善久之。

translations.literal: The Founder praised it as good for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai praised it at length.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗燕處，望見昶，輒斂容曰：「李秀才至矣。」
