translations.literal: The Founder once at leisure, seeing Chang in the distance, immediately composed his expression and said: "Scholar Li has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Once while at leisure Kublai saw Li Chang approaching and straightened up, saying, "Scholar Li is here."

sentences.zh: 其見敬禮如此。

translations.literal: Such was the respect and courtesy shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the respect in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 會嚴忠濟罷，以其弟忠範代之，忠範表請昶師事之，特授翰林侍講學士，行東平路緫管軍民同議官。

translations.literal: When Yan Zhongji was dismissed, his younger brother Zhongfan replaced him; Zhongfan memorialized requesting that Chang serve as his teacher; he was specially appointed Hanlin Attendant Lecturer and Acting Commissioner for Joint Deliberation on Military and Civil Affairs of Dongping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhongji was removed, his brother Zhongfan succeeded him. Zhongfan memorialized asking that Li Chang serve as his teacher, and Li Chang was specially appointed Hanlin Attendant Lecturer and acting commissioner for joint deliberation on military and civil affairs of Dongping Circuit.

sentences.zh: 昶條十二事，除宿弊。

translations.literal: Chang listed twelve items and remitted and abolished longstanding abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang submitted twelve reform proposals and remitted longstanding abuses.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，遷轉之制行，減併路、府、州、縣官員，於是謝事家居。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan the transfer system was implemented; officials of circuits, prefectures, departments, and counties were reduced and merged; thereupon he resigned from affairs and dwelt at home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1264 the rotation system took effect and circuit, prefecture, department, and county posts were cut and merged; Li Chang then resigned and lived at home.

sentences.zh: 五年，起為吏禮部尚書，品格條式、選舉禮文之事，多所裁定。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was raised to Minister of the Personnel and Rites Ministries; matters of rank standards and regulations, and examination rites and documents, were largely determined by him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1268 he was recalled as Minister of the Personnel and Rites Ministries and drafted much of the code on ranks and examination ritual.

sentences.zh: 凡議大政，宰相延置上座，傾聽其說。

translations.literal: Whenever great governance was deliberated, the chief minister would extend invitation and seat him in the place of honor, listening attentively to his views.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever major policy was debated, the chief minister seated him in the place of honor and listened closely.

sentences.zh: 六年，姦臣阿合馬議陞制國用使司為尚書省，昶請老以歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the treacherous minister Ahmad proposed elevating the Bureau of State Revenue to the Department of State Affairs; Chang requested old age and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1269, when the corrupt Ahmad proposed elevating the Bureau of State Revenue to a full Department of State Affairs, Li Chang asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔授南京路緫管兼府尹，不赴。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict appointed him Commissioner of Nanjing Circuit concurrently Prefect; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In 1270 he was appointed commissioner of Nanjing Circuit and concurrent prefect but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 八年，授山東東西道提刑按察使，務持大體，不事苛細，未幾致仕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Shandong Circuit for Punishment and Investigation; he strove to uphold the larger principles and did not pursue minutiae; before long he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1271 he was appointed surveillance commissioner for eastern and western Shandong, kept to broad principles rather than petty detail, and soon retired.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，昶年已八十二，復遣使征之，以老疾辭，賜田千畝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Chang was already eighty-two; envoys were again sent to summon him; he declined on grounds of old age and illness and was granted one thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285, when Li Chang was eighty-two, the court sent envoys to summon him again; he declined citing old age and illness and was granted a thousand mu of land.

sentences.zh: 二十六年卒，年八十有七。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died, age eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1289, aged eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 昶嘗集春秋諸家之說折中之，曰春秋左氏遺意二十卷；

translations.literal: Chang once gathered the various schools' interpretations of the Spring and Autumn Annals and reconciled them, titling the work The Remaining Intent of the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn in twenty juan;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang once collected the various schools' readings of the Spring and Autumn Annals and weighed them to a middle path, producing The Remaining Intent of the Zuo Tradition on the Spring and Autumn in twenty juan;

sentences.zh: 早年讀語、孟，見先儒之失，考訂成編，及得朱氏、張氏解，往往吻合，其書遂不復出。

translations.literal: In his early years reading the Analects and Mencius, he saw errors in earlier Confucian scholars and compiled corrections into a book; when he later obtained the commentaries of the Zhu and Zhang families, they often accorded with his own, so his book was never published again.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, while reading the Analects and Mencius, he found faults in earlier Confucian interpretations and compiled his own revisions; once he obtained the commentaries of the Zhu and Zhang schools, they often matched his work, and he never issued his book.

sentences.zh: 獨取孟子舊說新說矛盾者，參考歸一，附以己見，為孟子權衡遺說五卷。

translations.literal: Only regarding contradictory old and new interpretations of Mencius, he collated and unified them, added his own views, and produced Weighing the Remaining Interpretations of Mencius in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: He took only those points where old and new Mencius commentaries conflicted, reconciled them by reference, added his own judgment, and wrote Weighing the Remaining Interpretations of Mencius in five juan.

sentences.zh: 劉肅字才卿，威州洺水人。

translations.literal: Liu Su, courtesy name Caiqing, was a native of Ming River in Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Su, courtesy name Caiqing, came from Ming River in Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金興定二年詞賦進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding he passed the Jin civil examination in rhymed prose.
translations.idiomatic: In 1234 he passed the Jin metropolitan examination in the rhymed-prose category.

sentences.zh: 嘗為尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He once served as a clerk in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as a clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時有盜內藏官羅及珠，盜不時得，逮繫貨珠牙儈及藏吏，誣服者十一人。

translations.literal: At the time someone stole official silk and pearls from the inner treasury; the thief was not promptly caught, so pearl-dealing brokers and treasury clerks were arrested, and eleven confessed under duress.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone stole official silk and pearls from the inner treasury; the thief was not caught in time, and pearl brokers and treasury clerks were seized—eleven of them confessed under torture.

sentences.zh: 刑部議皆置極刑，肅執之曰：「盜無正贓，殺之冤。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice recommended capital punishment for all; Su held fast and said: "There is no actual stolen goods— to kill them would be unjust.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice recommended the death penalty for all of them, but Su insisted: "There is no recovered stolen property; to execute them would be a wrongful killing.

sentences.zh: 金主怒，有近侍夜見肅，具道其旨，肅曰：「辨析冤獄，我職也，惜一己而戕十一人之命，可乎！」

translations.literal: The Jin ruler was enraged; a close attendant visited Su at night and explained the sovereign's intent in full. Su said: "Examining and clarifying wrongful cases is my duty— would it be right to spare myself and destroy eleven lives!
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor was furious; a close attendant came to Su at night and laid out the sovereign's will. Su replied: "Sorting out wrongful cases is my duty. How could I save myself and take eleven lives!

sentences.zh: 明日，詣省辨愈力。

translations.literal: The next day he went to the Secretariat and argued his case with still greater force.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he went to the Secretariat and argued his case all the more forcefully.

sentences.zh: 右司郎中張天綱曰：「吾為汝具奏辨析之。」

translations.literal: You Simin Langzhong Zhang Tiangang said: "I will draw up a memorial for you setting forth the analysis.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiangang, Director in the Right Department, said: "I will prepare a memorial for you laying out the analysis.

sentences.zh: 奏入，金主悟，囚得不死。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; the Jin ruler came to understand, and the prisoners were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Jin emperor saw the point, and the prisoners were not put to death.

sentences.zh: 調新蔡令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 先時，縣賦民以牛多寡為差，民匿不耕，肅至，命樹畜繁者不加賦，民遂殷富。

translations.literal: Previously the county taxed the people according to the number of oxen they owned; people hid their livestock and stopped farming. When Su arrived, he ordered that those who raised many animals would not have extra tax levied, and the people grew prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the county assessed taxes according to how many oxen each household owned, so people hid their stock and left fields untilled. When Su took office, he ruled that households with large herds would not be taxed more heavily, and the people soon prospered.

sentences.zh: 瀕淮民有竄入宋境，籍為兵而優其糧，間有歸者，頗艱於衣食，時出怨言曰：「不如渡淮。」

translations.literal: People on the Huai frontier who slipped into Song territory were registered as soldiers and given favorable grain rations; some who returned found it hard to secure food and clothing, and from time to time murmured complaints: "Better to cross the Huai again.
translations.idiomatic: People living along the Huai who slipped into Song territory were enrolled as soldiers and given generous grain rations; some who came back struggled for food and clothing and now and then grumbled, "Better to cross the Huai again.

sentences.zh: 告者以謀叛論，肅曰：「淮限宋境，一水耳，果欲叛，不難往也，口雖言而心無實，準律當杖八十。」

translations.literal: Informants charged them with plotting rebellion. Su said: "The Huai is the only barrier to Song territory— just one river. If they truly wanted to rebel, crossing would not be difficult. Though their lips spoke thus, their hearts had no real intent; under the law they should receive eighty strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Informants accused them of plotting rebellion. Su said: "The Huai is all that separates us from Song—one river. If they truly meant to rebel, crossing would be easy enough. Their mouths spoke rashly, but their hearts had no real design; under the law they should receive eighty strokes of the cane.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: His memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 繼擢戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was subsequently promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 金亡，依東平嚴實，辟行尚書省左司員外郎，又改行軍萬戶府經歷。

translations.literal: After the Jin fell, he attached himself to Yan Shi of Dongping, was recruited as Assistant Director in the Left Department of the Provisional Secretariat, and then changed to administrator of the Military Ten-Thousand-Household Office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin dynasty fell, he joined Yan Shi of Dongping, was appointed Assistant Director in the Left Department of the Provisional Secretariat, and later became administrator of the Military Ten-Thousand-Household Office.

sentences.zh: 東平歲賦絲銀，復輸綿十萬兩、色絹萬匹，民不能堪，肅贊實奏罷之。

translations.literal: Dongping's annual levy in silk and silver additionally required one hundred thousand taels of cotton and ten thousand bolts of colored silk—the people could not bear it; Su supported Yan in memorializing to abolish these.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping's annual silk and silver levy also demanded one hundred thousand taels of cotton floss and ten thousand bolts of colored silk, which the people could not endure; Su helped Yan Shi memorialize to have these abolished.

sentences.zh: 壬子，世祖居潛邸，以肅為邢州安撫使，肅興鐵冶，及行楮幣，公私賴焉。

translations.literal: In the year renzi, while Kublai held his princely residence, Su was appointed pacification commissioner of Xingzhou; Su promoted iron smelting and the circulation of paper currency, on which public and private affairs both relied.
translations.idiomatic: In 1252, while Kublai still held his princely residence, Su was made pacification commissioner of Xingzhou; he revived iron smelting and introduced paper currency, and both public and private affairs came to depend on these measures.

sentences.zh: 肅性舒緩，有執守。

translations.literal: Su was unhurried in temperament but firm in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Su was easy in manner yet steadfast in what he upheld.

sentences.zh: 嘗集諸家易說，曰讀易備忘。

translations.literal: He once gathered various schools' commentaries on the Classic of Changes, titling it Notes for Reading the Yijing.
translations.idiomatic: He once collected commentaries on the Classic of Changes from various schools and called the work Notes for Reading the Changes.

sentences.zh: 後累贈推忠贊治功臣、榮祿大夫、上柱國、大司徒、邢國公，諡文獻。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously honored with the title of Meritorious Minister for Loyalty and Good Governance, Grand Master of Glorious Emolument, Upper Pillar of the State, Grand Minister of Education, Duke of Xing, and posthumous name Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously granted the titles Meritorious Minister for Loyalty and Good Governance, Grand Master of Glorious Emolument, Upper Pillar of the State, Grand Minister of Education, and Duke of Xing, with the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 子憲，禮部侍郎；

translations.literal: His son Xian was Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian served as Vice Minister of Rites;

sentences.zh: 愻，大名路緫管。

translations.literal: Xun was administrator of Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xun became administrator of Daming Circuit.

sentences.zh: 孫賡，翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: His grandson Geng was academician-expositor-in-chief of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Geng rose to Hanlin academician-expositor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 王思廉

translations.literal: Wang Silian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Silian

sentences.zh: 王思廉字仲常，真定獲鹿人。

translations.literal: Wang Silian, courtesy name Zhongchang, was a native of Huolu in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Silian, courtesy name Zhongchang, came from Huolu in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 幼師太原元好問，既冠，張德耀宣撫河東，辟掌書記，復謝歸。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Yuan Haowen of Taiyuan; after reaching manhood, when Zhang Deyao pacified Hedong, he was recruited as chief recorder but declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied with Yuan Haowen of Taiyuan; after coming of age, when Zhang Deyao pacified Hedong and recruited him as chief secretary, he declined and went home.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，董文忠薦之，世祖問文忠曰：「汝何由知王思廉賢﹖」對曰：「鄉人之善者稱之也。」

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan, Dong Wenzhong recommended him. The Emperor asked Wenzhong, "How do you know that Wang Silian is worthy?" He replied, "Good people in the countryside speak well of him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1273, Dong Wenzhong recommended him. Kublai asked Wenzhong, "How do you know Wang Silian is worthy?" He answered, "The good people of the countryside praise him.

sentences.zh: 遂召見，授符寶局掌書。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience and appointed chief secretary of the Bureau of Seals and Talismans.
translations.idiomatic: Silian was then summoned to audience and appointed chief secretary of the Bureau of Seals and Talismans.

sentences.zh: 十三年，姚樞舉為昭文館待制，遷奉訓大夫、符寶局直長。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Yao Shu recommended him as compiler of the Hall of Broad Culture; he was transferred to Grand Master for Fostering Instruction and director of the Bureau of Seals and Talismans.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276, Yao Shu recommended him as a compiler of the Hall for the Propagation of Literature; he was promoted to Grand Master for Fostering Instruction and made director of the Bureau of Seals and Talismans.

sentences.zh: 十四年，改翰林待制，嘗進讀通鑑，至唐太宗有殺魏徵語，及長孫皇后進諫事，帝命內官引至皇后閤，講衍其說，后曰：「是誠有益於宸衷。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was changed to Hanlin compiler; he once lectured from the Comprehensive Mirror, reaching the passage where Emperor Taizong of Tang spoke of killing Wei Zheng and where Empress Zhangsun offered remonstrance; the Emperor ordered palace attendants to escort him to the empress's chamber to expound on these points. The empress said, "This is truly beneficial to the imperial mind.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 he was transferred to Hanlin compiler. Once, while lecturing from the Comprehensive Mirror, he came to the passage where Tang Taizong spoke of killing Wei Zheng and where Empress Zhangsun remonstrated with him. The Emperor had palace attendants escort Silian to the empress's chamber to develop the point. The empress said, "This truly benefits the imperial heart.

sentences.zh: 爾宜擇善言進講，慎勿以瀆辭煩上聽也。」

translations.literal: You should select good words when lecturing; take care not to annoy His Majesty's ears with irreverent speech.
translations.idiomatic: Choose good words when you lecture, and take care not to weary the Emperor's ears with impertinent language.

sentences.zh: 每侍讀，帝命御史大夫玉速帖木兒、太師月赤察兒、御史中丞撒里蠻、翰林學士承旨掇立察等，咸聽受焉。

translations.literal: Each time he lectured, the Emperor ordered Grand Censor Yisutiemuer, Grand Preceptor Yuechichaer, Censor-in-Chief Salam, Hanlin academician-expositor Dielicha, and others all to listen and receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lectured, the Emperor ordered the Grand Censor Yisutemur, Grand Preceptor Yechichar, Censor-in-Chief Salam, Hanlin expositor Dielicha, and others all to listen.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗御延春閣，大賚群臣，俾十人為列以進，思廉偶在衛士之列，帝責董文忠曰：「思廉儒臣，豈宜列衛士！」

translations.literal: The Emperor once held court in the Ever-Spring Pavilion and lavished gifts on the assembled ministers, ordering them to advance in columns of ten. By chance Silian happened to be in a column with the guards. The Emperor reproached Dong Wenzhong, saying, "Silian is a Confucian official— how can he be ranked with the guards!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, when the Emperor held court in the Ever-Spring Pavilion and showered gifts on the ministers, ordering them to advance in columns of ten, Silian happened to stand in a guard's column. The Emperor rebuked Dong Wenzhong: "Silian is a Confucian minister—how can he be placed among the guards!"

sentences.zh: 十八年，進中順大夫、典瑞少監。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Proper Submission and vice director of the Office of Ceremonial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he was promoted to Grand Master of Proper Submission and vice director of the Office of Ceremonial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 十九年，帝幸白海，時千戶王著，矯殺奸臣阿合馬於大都，辭連樞副密使張易。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Emperor traveled to the White Sea; at that time the chiliarch Wang Zhuo, feigning authority, killed the corrupt minister Ahmad in Dadu; the case implicated Zhang Yi, vice director of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1282, while the Emperor was at the White Sea, the chiliarch Wang Zhuo, acting under false authority, killed the corrupt minister Ahmad in Dadu; the case implicated Zhang Yi, vice director of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 帝召思廉至行殿，屏左右，問曰：「張易反，若知之乎﹖」對曰：「未詳也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Silian to the traveling hall, dismissed attendants, and asked, "Zhang Yi has rebelled— did you know of it?" He replied, "I do not know the details.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Silian to the traveling hall, sent away attendants, and asked, "Zhang Yi has rebelled—did you know?" He replied, "I do not yet know the particulars.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「反已反已，何未詳也﹖」思廉徐奏曰：「僭號改元謂之反，亡入他國謂之叛，群聚山林賊害民物謂之亂，張易之事，臣實不能詳也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "He has already rebelled, rebelled— what is there not to know?" Silian slowly submitted, "Proclaiming a title and changing the era name is called rebellion; fleeing to another state is called treason; gathering in mountains and forests and robbing the people is called disorder. As for Zhang Yi's affair, your minister truly cannot be certain of the details.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "He has rebelled, rebelled—what is there not to know?" Silian answered slowly, "Usurping a title and changing the reign name is called rebellion; fleeing to another state is called treason; banding together in the hills and preying on the people is called disorder. As for Zhang Yi's case, your servant truly cannot say what it is.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕自即位以來，如李璮之不臣，豈以我若漢高帝、趙太祖，遽陟帝位者乎﹖」思廉曰：「陛下神聖天縱，前代之君不足比也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Since my accession, such as Li Tan's disloyalty— do you think it is because, like Emperor Gaozu of Han or Emperor Taizu of Zhao, I abruptly ascended the throne?" Silian said, "Your Majesty is divinely sage and heaven-endowed; rulers of former ages cannot compare.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Since I took the throne, cases like Li Tan's disloyalty—do you think they arise because, like Han Gaozu or Song Taizu, I seized the throne too hastily?" Silian said, "Your Majesty is divinely sage and heaven-taught; no ruler of earlier ages can compare.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「朕往者，有問於竇默，其應如響，蓋心口不相違，故不思而得，朕今有問汝，能然乎﹖且張易所為，張仲謙知之否﹖」思廉即對曰：「仲謙不知。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed, "In the past when I questioned Dou Mo, his answers rang like echoes— his heart and mouth did not conflict, so he answered without deliberation. I now question you— can you do the same? And did Zhang Zhongqian know of Zhang Yi's actions?" Silian immediately replied, "Zhongqian did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sighed, "When I once questioned Dou Mo, his answers came like echoes—heart and mouth never parted, so he answered without thinking. I question you now: can you do the same? And did Zhang Zhongqian know what Zhang Yi was doing?" Silian answered at once, "Zhongqian did not know.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何以明之﹖」對曰：「二人不相安，臣故知其不知也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "How do you know this?" He replied, "The two were not on good terms— therefore I know he did not know."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "How do you know?" He replied, "The two could not abide each other, so I know he did not know."

sentences.zh: 二十年，陞太監。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1283 he was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 思廉以儒素進，帝眷注優渥。

translations.literal: Silian advanced through plain Confucian virtue, and the Emperor's favor was exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: Silian had risen as a plain Confucian scholar, and the Emperor's regard for him was unusually warm.

sentences.zh: 嘗疾，賜御藥，顧問安否；

translations.literal: When he fell ill, the Emperor granted imperial medicine and inquired after his condition;
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, the Emperor sent imperial medicine and asked after his health;

sentences.zh: 扈蹕，失所乘馬，給內廄馬五匹；

translations.literal: When escorting the imperial procession he lost his mount, and was given five horses from the imperial stables;
translations.idiomatic: while attending the imperial procession he lost his horse and was given five mounts from the imperial stables;

sentences.zh: 盜竊所賜玉帶，更以玉帶賜之。

translations.literal: When the jade belt he had been granted was stolen, he was given another jade belt in its place.
translations.idiomatic: when the jade belt he had been granted was stolen, the Emperor gave him another jade belt.

sentences.zh: 裕宗居東宮，思廉進曰：「殿下府中，宜建學官，俾左右近侍，嘗親正學，必能裨輔明德。」

translations.literal: While Crown Prince Zhenjin resided in the Eastern Palace, Silian submitted, "Within Your Highness's household, a school should be established so that attendants close at hand may often engage in proper learning— this will surely aid in cultivating bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: While Crown Prince Zhenjin lived in the Eastern Palace, Silian submitted, "Your Highness's household should establish a school so that those close at hand may regularly pursue proper learning; that will surely help cultivate bright virtue.

sentences.zh: 裕宗然之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 裕宗嘗欲買甲第賜思廉，思廉固辭。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince once wished to purchase a fine mansion to grant Silian, but Silian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince once wanted to buy a fine mansion for Silian, but Silian firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改嘉議大夫、同知大都留守，兼少府監事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was changed to Grand Master for Glorious Counsel, associate chief steward of Dadu, and concurrently vice director of the Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: In 1286 he was made Grand Master for Glorious Counsel, associate chief steward of Dadu, and concurrently vice director of the Palace Workshop.

sentences.zh: 藩王乃顏叛，帝親征，思廉間謂留守段貞曰：「藩王反側，地大故也，漢鼂錯削地之策，實為良圖，盍為上言之。」

translations.literal: When the frontier prince Nayan rebelled and the Emperor personally campaigned against him, Silian privately said to Chief Steward Duan Zhen, "A frontier prince's instability arises from his vast territory. The Han minister Chao Cuo's policy of carving off lands was truly a sound plan— why not speak of it to the sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier prince Nayan rebelled and the Emperor marched in person, Silian privately told Chief Steward Duan Zhen, "A frontier prince turns restless because his domain is too large. Chao Cuo's Han policy of reducing fiefs was a sound plan—why not put it before the throne?

sentences.zh: 貞見帝，遂以聞，帝曰：「汝何能出是言也﹖」貞以思廉對，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Zhen saw the Emperor and reported this. The Emperor said, "How could you come out with such words?" Zhen named Silian, and the Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen saw the Emperor and reported this. The Emperor said, "How did you come to speak such words?" Zhen named Silian, and the Emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷正議大夫、樞密院判官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Grand Master for Direct Counsel and judge of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1292 he was transferred to Grand Master for Direct Counsel and judge of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，成宗即位，遷中奉大夫、翰林學士，仍樞密院判官，以病歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, when Emperor Chengzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Grand Master for Proper Service and Hanlin academician, still serving as Privy Council judge, and returned home due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1297, when Emperor Chengzong took the throne, he was made Grand Master for Proper Service and Hanlin academician while retaining his Privy Council judgeship, then returned home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 三年，起為工部尚書，拜征東行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled as Minister of Works and appointed vice administrator of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299 he was recalled as Minister of Works and appointed vice administrator of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七年，緫管大名路。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was administrator of Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1303 he became administrator of Daming Circuit.

sentences.zh: 八年，召為集賢學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned to be academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1304 he was summoned to serve as academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授正奉大夫、太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was granted Grand Master for Upholding the State and Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1307 he was granted the title Grand Master for Upholding the State and appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，以翰林學士承旨、資善大夫致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, he retired as Hanlin academician-expositor-in-chief with the title Grand Master for Nurturing Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he retired with the titles Hanlin academician-expositor-in-chief and Grand Master for Nurturing Goodness.

sentences.zh: 延祐七年卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yanyou he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1320, aged eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈翰林學士承旨、資德大夫、河南江北等處行中書省右丞、上護軍，追封恒山郡公，諡文恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Hanlin academician-expositor-in-chief, Grand Master of Virtuous Merit, right vice administrator of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, Upper Guardian General of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Hengshan with posthumous name Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted Hanlin academician-expositor-in-chief, Grand Master of Virtuous Merit, and right vice administrator of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, with the rank Upper Guardian General; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Hengshan and given the posthumous name Wengong.

sentences.zh: 李謙字受益，鄆之東阿人。

translations.literal: Li Qian, courtesy name Shouyi, was from Dong'e in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qian, courtesy name Shouyi, came from Dong'e in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖元，以醫著名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuan was famed as a physician.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuan was renowned as a physician.

sentences.zh: 父唐佐，性恬退，不喜仕進。

translations.literal: His father Tangzuo was placid and retiring by nature, taking no pleasure in official advancement.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tangzuo was quiet and withdrawn by nature and took no pleasure in pursuing office.

sentences.zh: 謙幼有成人風，始就學，日記數千言，為賦有聲，與徐世隆、孟祺、閻復齊名，而謙為首。

translations.literal: Qian as a child already had the bearing of a mature man; when he first began study he could recite several thousand words daily; his fu verse won renown; he was ranked with Xu Shilong, Meng Qi, and Yan Fu, and Qian stood first among them.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Qian already had the bearing of a grown man; when he first took up study he could memorize several thousand words a day, and his fu verse won fame. He was ranked with Xu Shilong, Meng Qi, and Yan Fu, and Qian stood first among them.

sentences.zh: 為東平府教授，生徒四集，累官萬戶府經歷，復教授東平。

translations.literal: He served as professor of Dongping Prefecture, with students gathering from all directions; he accumulated offices up to administrator of the Ten-Thousand-Household Office, then again taught in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He served as professor of Dongping Prefecture, where students gathered from all quarters; he rose to administrator of the Ten-Thousand-Household Office, then returned to teach in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 先時，教授無俸，郡斂儒戶銀百兩備束脩，謙辭曰：「家幸非甚貧者，豈可聚貨以自殖乎！」

translations.literal: Previously professors received no salary; the prefecture collected one hundred taels of silver from Confucian households for teacher's fees. Qian declined, saying, "My household is fortunately not very poor— how could I gather wealth to enrich myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Previously professors received no salary, and the prefecture collected one hundred taels of silver from Confucian households for their stipends. Qian refused, saying, "My family is fortunately not very poor—how could I amass goods to enrich myself!"

sentences.zh: 翰林學士王磐以謙名聞，召為應奉翰林文字，一時制誥，多出其手。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Wang Pan, having heard of Qian's reputation, summoned him as Hanlin draftsman on call; for a time most imperial proclamations came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Wang Pan, hearing of Qian's reputation, summoned him as a Hanlin draftsman on call; for a time most imperial edicts and proclamations came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年，陞待制，扈駕至上都，賜以銀壺、藤枕。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to compiler; he escorted the imperial procession to Shangdu and was granted a silver flagon and a rattan pillow.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was promoted to compiler, accompanied the imperial procession to Shangdu, and was granted a silver flagon and a rattan pillow.

sentences.zh: 十八年，陞直學士，為太子左諭德，侍裕宗於東宮。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to associate academician and served as Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, attending Crown Prince Zhenjin in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he was promoted to associate academician and appointed Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, attending Crown Prince Zhenjin in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 陳十事：曰正心，曰睦親，曰崇儉，曰幾諫，曰戢兵，曰親賢，曰尚文，曰定律，曰正名，曰革弊。

translations.literal: He set forth ten matters: to rectify the heart-mind, to harmonize with kin, to esteem frugality, to offer subtle remonstrance, to restrain the military, to esteem the worthy, to honor culture, to fix the laws, to rectify names, and to reform abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth ten counsels: rectifying the heart, harmonizing with kin, honoring frugality, offering timely remonstrance, restraining the military, esteeming the worthy, honoring culture, fixing the laws, rectifying names, and reforming abuses.

sentences.zh: 裕宗崩，世祖又命傅成宗於潛邸，所至以謙自隨。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhenjin died, Kublai again ordered Qian to tutor Chengzong at his princely residence, taking Qian with him wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Zhenjin died, Kublai again ordered Qian to instruct Chengzong at his princely residence and took Qian with him wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 世祖深加器重，嘗賜坐便殿，飲群臣酒，世祖曰：「聞卿不飲，然能為朕強飲乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor held him in deep regard; once granted a seat in the informal hall while the ministers drank wine, Kublai said, "I hear you do not drink— yet can you drink a forced cup for me?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held him in the highest regard. Once, seated with him in the informal hall while the ministers drank wine, Kublai said, "I hear you do not drink—yet will you drink a cup for my sake?

sentences.zh: 因賜蒲萄酒一鍾，曰：「此極醉人，恐汝不勝。」

translations.literal: He therefore granted him a bowl of grape wine, saying, "This is exceedingly intoxicating— I fear you cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him a bowl of grape wine and said, "This is very strong—I fear you cannot stand it.

sentences.zh: 即令三近侍扶掖使出。

translations.literal: He at once ordered three close attendants to support and escort him out.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered three close attendants to support him and escort him out.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，以足疾辭歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he requested leave and returned home due to foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1289 he asked to retire and returned home because of a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗即位，驛召至上都。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, when Chengzong ascended the throne, he was summoned by relay post to Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1294, when Chengzong took the throne, he was summoned by relay post to Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 既見，勞曰：「朕知卿有疾，然京師去家不遠，且多良醫，能愈疾。

translations.literal: After the audience, the Emperor comforted him, saying, "I know you have an illness; yet the capital is not far from your home, and there are many skilled physicians who can cure your ailment.
translations.idiomatic: After the audience the Emperor comforted him, saying, "I know you are ill, but the capital is not far from your home, and there are many skilled physicians who can cure you.

sentences.zh: 卿當與謀國政，餘不以勞卿也。」

translations.literal: You should join in deliberating on state affairs— I will not burden you with other duties.
translations.idiomatic: You should join in deliberating on state affairs; I will not burden you with other labors.

sentences.zh: 陞學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to academician.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was promoted to academician.

sentences.zh: 元貞初，引疾還家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanzhen, he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanzhen era he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 大德六年，召為翰林承旨，以年七十一，乞致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dade he was summoned as Hanlin expositor-in-chief; at age seventy-one he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1302 he was summoned as Hanlin expositor-in-chief, but at seventy-one he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 九年，又召。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 he was summoned again.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，給半俸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was granted half salary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was granted half salary.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，徵為太子少傅，謙皆力辭。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, Qian was recruited as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; Qian firmly declined on each occasion.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, Qian was invited to serve as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, but he firmly declined each time.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，召十六人，謙居其首。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, sixteen men were summoned; Qian stood first among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, sixteen men were summoned, and Qian stood first among them.

sentences.zh: 乃力疾見帝于行在，疏言九事，其略曰：「正心術以正百官，崇孝治以先天下，選賢能以居輔相之位，廣視聽以通上下之情，恤貧乏以重邦家之本，課農桑以豐衣食之源，興學校以廣人材之路，頒律令使民不犯，練士卒居安慮危。

translations.literal: He forced himself, despite illness, to see the Emperor at the traveling residence and submitted a memorial setting forth nine matters; the gist read: "Rectify the heart-mind and methods to rectify the hundred officials; honor filial governance to put the empire first; select the worthy and able for positions as chief ministers; broaden sight and hearing to connect sentiment between above and below; relieve poverty to reinforce the foundation of the realm; assess farming and sericulture to enrich the source of food and clothing; establish schools to widen the path for human talent; promulgate laws and ordinances so the people will not transgress; train soldiers—in peace, consider danger.
translations.idiomatic: Despite his illness he forced himself to see the Emperor at the traveling palace and submitted a memorial on nine matters. Its gist ran: "Rectify the ruler's heart and methods to rectify the hundred officials; honor filial governance to put the empire first; choose the worthy and able for chief-ministerial posts; broaden sight and hearing to connect sentiment above and below; relieve poverty to strengthen the state's foundation; assess farming and sericulture to enrich the source of food and clothing; establish schools to widen the path for talent; promulgate laws so the people will not transgress; drill soldiers—in peace, think of danger.

sentences.zh: 至於振肅紀綱、糾察內外，臺憲之官尤當選素著清望、深明治體、不事苛細者為之。」

translations.literal: As for invigorating discipline, investigating inner and outer affairs—for censorate and surveillance posts one ought especially to choose men of established pure reputation who deeply understand governance and do not pursue minutiae.
translations.idiomatic: As for restoring discipline and investigating affairs within and without, censorate and surveillance posts should especially be filled by men of long-standing pure reputation who deeply understand governance and do not traffic in petty detail.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 遷集賢大學士、榮祿大夫，致仕，加賜銀一百五十兩，金織幣及帛各三匹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Academician of Scholarly Worthies and Grand Master of Glorious Emolument, retired from office, and additionally granted one hundred fifty taels of silver, three bolts each of gold brocade tribute cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Academician of Scholarly Worthies and Grand Master of Glorious Emolument, retired from office, and was additionally granted one hundred fifty taels of silver plus three bolts each of gold brocade tribute cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 歸，卒于家，年七十九。

translations.literal: Returning home, he died at his house, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he died there, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 謙文章醇厚有古風，不尚浮巧，學者宗之，號野齋先生。

translations.literal: Qian's essays were rich and mellow with an antique air; he did not favor ornate cleverness; scholars took him as their model and called him Master of the Wilderness Studio.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's writing was rich and mellow, with an antique cast; he did not prize flashy cleverness. Scholars looked to him as their model and called him Master Yezai.

sentences.zh: 子偘，官至大名路緫管。

translations.literal: His son Kan reached the office of administrator of Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan rose to administrator of Daming Circuit.

sentences.zh: 徐世隆

translations.literal: Xu Shilong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shilong

sentences.zh: 徐世隆字威卿，陳州西華人。

translations.literal: Xu Shilong, courtesy name Weiqing, was a native of Xihua in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shilong, courtesy name Weiqing, came from Xihua in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，登金正大四年進士第，辟為縣令。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he passed the Jin metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Zhengda and was recruited as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he passed the Jin metropolitan examination in 1227 and was recruited to serve as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 其父戒世隆曰：「汝年少，學未至，毋急仕進，更當讀書，多識往事，以益智識，俟三十入官，未晚也。」

translations.literal: His father admonished Shilong, saying, "You are young; your learning has not yet reached completion. Do not be eager to advance in office. You should further study, learn much of past events to increase wisdom and knowledge, and wait until thirty to enter office—it would not be late."
translations.idiomatic: His father admonished him: "You are young and your learning is not yet complete. Do not rush into official life. Keep reading, learn more of past events to sharpen your mind, and wait until you are thirty to take office—that will be soon enough."

sentences.zh: 世隆遂辭官，益篤于學。

translations.literal: Shilong thereupon resigned office and became still more devoted to study.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong resigned his post and devoted himself even more deeply to study.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，擢燕京等路宣撫使，世隆以新民善俗為務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Yanjing and other circuits. Shilong made civilizing the people and improving customs his task.
translations.idiomatic: In 1260 he was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Yanjing and other circuits. Shilong made it his business to settle the people and improve local customs.

sentences.zh: 中書省檄諸路養禁衛之羸馬，數以萬計，芻秣與其什器，前期戒備。

translations.literal: The Secretariat dispatched orders to all circuits to provision the emaciated horses of the imperial guard—numbering in the tens of thousands—requiring advance preparation of fodder and their equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat ordered every circuit to provision the imperial guard's emaciated horses—numbering in the tens of thousands—requiring fodder and equipment to be readied well in advance.

sentences.zh: 世隆曰：「國馬牧於北方，往年無飼於南者。

translations.literal: Shilong said, "The state's horses are pastured in the north; in previous years none were fed in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said, "The empire's horses are kept in the north; in past years none were provisioned in the south.

sentences.zh: 上新臨天下，京畿根本地，煩擾之事，必不為之。

translations.literal: The Emperor has newly come to rule all under Heaven; this is the fundamental territory of the capital region—a troublesome matter like this, he surely will not undertake it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor has only just begun to rule; the capital region is the empire's heartland, and he will surely not burden it with such a vexing task.

sentences.zh: 馬將不來。」

translations.literal: The horses will not come."
translations.idiomatic: The horses will not come."

sentences.zh: 吏白：「此軍需也，其責勿輕。」

translations.literal: A clerk reported, "This is a military requisition—the responsibility must not be treated lightly."
translations.idiomatic: A clerk protested, "This is a military requisition—the responsibility is not to be taken lightly."

sentences.zh: 世隆曰：「責當我坐。」

translations.literal: Shilong said, "The responsibility should rest on me."
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said, "Let the responsibility rest on me."

sentences.zh: 遂弗為備，馬果不至。

translations.literal: He therefore made no preparations, and the horses indeed did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He made no preparations, and as he had predicted, the horses never came.

sentences.zh: 清滄鹽課，前政虧不及額，世隆綜覈之，得增羨若干，賜銀三十鋌。

translations.literal: For the salt tax of Qing-Cang, the previous administration fell short of quota; Shilong comprehensively audited it and obtained an increase above surplus of a certain amount, and was granted thirty ingots of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing-Cang salt levy had fallen short under the previous administration. Shilong conducted a full audit and recovered a substantial surplus, for which he was rewarded with thirty ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 二年，移治順天，歲饑，世隆發廩貸之，全活甚衆。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to administer Shuntian; famine struck that year, and Shilong opened the granaries and lent grain, saving the lives of very many.
translations.idiomatic: In 1261 he was transferred to administer Shuntian. That year famine struck, and Shilong opened the granaries to lend grain, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣撫司罷，世隆還東平，請增宮縣大樂、文武二舞，令舊工教習，以備大祀，制可。

translations.literal: In the third year the Pacification Commission was abolished; Shilong returned to Dongping, requested adding the grand music and civil and military two dances of the palace counties, ordered old craftsmen to instruct in practice to prepare for the great sacrifices—the decree was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 the Pacification Commission was abolished and Shilong returned to Dongping. He petitioned to add the grand music and civil and military dances of the palace counties, had veteran musicians train performers for the great state sacrifices, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 除世隆太常卿以掌之，兼提舉本路學校事。

translations.literal: Shilong was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonial to manage it, and concurrently placed in charge of schools in his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonial to oversee these matters and concurrently put in charge of schools in his circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，世祖問堯、舜、禹、湯為君之道，世隆取書所載帝王事以對，帝喜曰：「汝為朕直解進讀，我將聽之。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year Kublai asked about the ways of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang as rulers; Shilong drew on what the classics record of emperors and kings to answer. The Emperor was pleased and said, "You shall prepare plain explanations for me to read aloud—I will listen."
translations.idiomatic: In 1263 Kublai asked about the principles by which Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang had ruled. Shilong answered by citing what the classics record of emperors and kings. The Emperor was pleased and said, "Prepare a plain commentary for me to read—I will listen."

sentences.zh: 書成，帝命翰林承旨安藏譯寫以進。

translations.literal: When the book was complete, the Emperor ordered Hanlin expositor-in-chief Ancang to translate and copy it for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, the Emperor ordered Hanlin expositor-in-chief Ancang to translate it and have it copied for presentation.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，遷翰林侍講學士，兼太常卿，朝廷大政諮訪而後行，詔命典冊多出其手。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to Hanlin Lecturing Academician, concurrently Grand Master of Ceremonial; great matters of court policy were consulted with him before action, and imperial edicts and canonical documents often came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1264 he was promoted to Hanlin Lecturing Academician while retaining the post of Grand Master of Ceremonial. Major state affairs were referred to him before action was taken, and many edicts and ceremonial documents issued from his hand.

sentences.zh: 世隆奏：「陛下帝中國，當行中國事。

translations.literal: Shilong memorialized: "Your Majesty rules China—it is appropriate to conduct Chinese affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty reigns over China; you should govern according to Chinese ways.

sentences.zh: 事之大者，首惟祭祀，祭必有廟。」

translations.literal: Among great matters, sacrifice comes first, and sacrifice requires a temple."
translations.idiomatic: Of great affairs, sacrifice comes first—and sacrifice requires a temple."

sentences.zh: 因以圖上，乞敕有司以時興建，從之，踰年而廟成。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a diagram, requesting that the appropriate offices be ordered to build it in due time. The request was approved; within the year the temple was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a design and asked that the responsible offices be ordered to build it promptly. The request was granted, and within a year the temple was completed.

sentences.zh: 遂迎祖宗神御，奉安太室，而大饗禮成。

translations.literal: Thereupon the spirit tablets of the imperial ancestors were received and installed in the Grand Chamber, and the great offering ceremony was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial ancestral tablets were then enshrined in the Grand Chamber, and the great state offering was performed.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賞賜優渥。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and rewarded him with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 俄兼戶部侍郎，承詔議立三省，遂定內外官制上之。

translations.literal: Shortly he concurrently served as Vice Minister of Revenue; receiving an edict to deliberate on establishing the Three Secretariats, he then fixed the inner and outer official system and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also appointed Vice Minister of Revenue. Ordered to deliberate on establishing the Three Secretariats, he drew up the inner and outer bureaucracy and submitted his plan.

sentences.zh: 時朝儀未立，世隆奏曰；

translations.literal: At that time court ceremony had not yet been established; Shilong memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual had not yet been established. Shilong memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「今四海一家，萬國會同，朝廷之禮，不可不肅，宜定百官朝會儀。」

translations.literal: "Now all within the four seas are one family and the myriad states have joined in unity—court ceremony cannot but be solemn; it is fitting to fix the ceremony for officials' court assemblies."
translations.idiomatic: "Now all under Heaven is one family and the myriad states united. Court ceremony must be dignified—official assembly ritual should be fixed."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was accepted.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷吏部尚書，世隆以銓選無可守之法，為撰選曹八議。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Minister of Personnel; Shilong, finding that selection and appointment had no fixed rules to follow, drafted the Eight Deliberations for the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In 1270 he was promoted to Minister of Personnel. Finding that appointments lacked fixed standards, he drafted the Eight Deliberations for the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 九年，乞補外，佩虎符，為東昌路緫管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he requested an outside appointment, was granted the tiger tally, and served as administrator of Dongchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1272 he asked for a provincial appointment, was granted the tiger tally, and became administrator of Dongchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至郡，專務以德率下，不事鞭箠，吏不忍欺，民亦化服，期年而政成，郡人頌之。

translations.literal: Reaching the prefecture, he devoted himself solely to leading subordinates by virtue, did not rely on whips and caning; clerks could not bear to deceive him, and the people also were transformed and submitted. Within a year governance was accomplished, and the people of the circuit praised him.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he led by moral example and never relied on the lash. Clerks shrank from deceiving him, and the people came around as well. Within a year his administration was complete, and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 十四年，起為山東提刑按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was recalled as Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 he was recalled to serve as Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 時有妖言獄，所司逮捕凡數百人，世隆剖析詿誤者十八九，悉縱遣之。

translations.literal: At that time there was a case of heterodox speech; the responsible offices arrested several hundred people in all. Shilong sifted out those who had been misled—eight or nine in ten—and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a case involving seditious talk, and the authorities had arrested several hundred people. Shilong found that eight or nine in ten had been misled and released them all.

sentences.zh: 十五年，移淮東。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was transferred to eastern Huai.

sentences.zh: 宋將許瓊家童，告瓊匿官庫財，有司繫其妻孥征之。

translations.literal: A household slave of Song general Xu Qiong reported that Qiong had concealed property from the government storehouse; the responsible offices imprisoned his wife and children to collect it.
translations.idiomatic: A household slave of the Song general Xu Qiong accused him of hiding government-storehouse property. The authorities imprisoned Qiong's wife and children to recover the goods.

sentences.zh: 世隆曰：「瓊所匿者，故宋之物，豈得與今盜官財者同論耶﹖」同僚不從，世隆獨抗章辯明，行臺是之，釋不問。

translations.literal: Shilong said, "What Qiong concealed were goods of the former Song—how can this be judged the same as stealing government property today?" His colleagues did not agree, but Shilong alone submitted a memorial to explain and clear the matter; the regional office approved, and Qiong was released without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said, "What Qiong hid were possessions of the former Song—how can that be treated like stealing government property now?" His colleagues disagreed, but Shilong alone submitted a memorial arguing the point. The regional headquarters agreed and released him without further prosecution.

sentences.zh: 會征日本，世隆上疏諫止，語頗剴切，當路者不即以聞，已而帝意悟，其事亦寢。

translations.literal: When an expedition against Japan was planned, Shilong submitted a memorial to remonstrate and stop it; his words were quite forceful. Those in power did not immediately report it, but afterward the Emperor's mind came round and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When an expedition against Japan was proposed, Shilong submitted a forceful memorial urging against it. Those in power did not report it at once, but the Emperor later changed his mind and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十七年，召為翰林學士，又召為集賢學士，皆以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was summoned as Hanlin Academician and again summoned as Academician of Scholarly Worthies; on each occasion he declined citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1280 he was summoned as Hanlin Academician and again as Academician of Scholarly Worthies, but declined both appointments citing illness.

sentences.zh: 世隆儀觀魁梧，襟度宏博，慈祥樂易。

translations.literal: Shilong had a tall and imposing appearance, broad and capacious bearing, and was kindly, pleasant, and easygoing.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was tall and imposing, broad-minded, kindly, and easygoing.

sentences.zh: 人忤之，無慍色。

translations.literal: When people offended him he showed no sign of anger.
translations.idiomatic: When people crossed him he showed no anger.

sentences.zh: 喜賓客，樂施與，明習前代典故，尤精律令，善決疑獄。

translations.literal: He delighted in guests, enjoyed giving; he was well versed in precedents of earlier dynasties, especially skilled in statutes and ordinances, and adept at resolving doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: He loved hosting guests and giving freely. He was well versed in earlier dynastic precedent, especially skilled in law, and adept at resolving difficult cases.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，安童再入相，奏世隆雖老，尚可用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Antong again entered the chancellorship and memorialized that although Shilong was old he could still be used.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 Antong returned to the chancellorship and recommended Shilong, saying that though old he was still fit for service.

sentences.zh: 遣使召之，仍以老病辭，附奏便宜九事。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to summon him; he again declined citing old age and illness, and appended a memorial on nine expedient measures.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to summon him, but he again declined on account of age and illness, appending a memorial on nine practical measures.

sentences.zh: 賜田十頃。

translations.literal: He was granted ten qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted ten qing of land.

sentences.zh: 時年八十，卒。

translations.literal: He was then eighty years old and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty when he died.

sentences.zh: 所著有瀛洲集百卷、文集若干卷。

translations.literal: His written works included one hundred juan of the Yingzhou Collection and several juan of collected essays.
translations.idiomatic: His works included the hundred-juan Yingzhou Collection and several juan of collected essays.

sentences.zh: 孟祺字德卿，宿州符離人。

translations.literal: Meng Qi, courtesy name Deqing, was a native of Fuli in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qi, courtesy name Deqing, came from Fuli in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 世以財雄鄉里。

translations.literal: For generations his family was wealthy and dominated the village.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family was the wealthiest in the district.

sentences.zh: 父仁，業儒，有節行。

translations.literal: His father Ren pursued Confucian studies and possessed integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren was a scholar of Confucian learning and a man of moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，北渡，寓濟州魚臺，州帥石天祿禮之，辟兼詳議府事。

translations.literal: In the renchen year he crossed north, lodged at Yutai in Jizhou; the prefectural commander Shi Tianlu treated him with ceremony and recruited him to concurrently serve in the Detailed Deliberation Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1232 he crossed north and settled at Yutai in Jizhou. The prefectural commander Shi Tianlu received him with honor and appointed him to the Detailed Deliberation Office.

sentences.zh: 祺幼敏悟，善騎射，早知問學，侍父徙居東平。

translations.literal: Qi from youth was sharp and perceptive, skilled at horseback archery, early understood learning and questioning; accompanying his father he moved to reside at Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Qi was bright and quick, skilled at horsemanship and archery, and showed an early taste for learning. He accompanied his father to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 時嚴實修學校，招生徒，立考試法，祺就試，登上選，辟掌書記。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Shi repaired the school, recruited students, and established an examination method; Qi took the test, placed in the top selection, and was recruited as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi was then rebuilding the school, enrolling students, and instituting examinations. Qi took the exam, ranked at the top, and was appointed chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 廉希憲、宋子貞皆器遇之，以聞于朝，擢國史院編修官。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian and Song Zizhen both valued and favored him, reported him to court, and he was promoted to compiler in the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian and Song Zizhen both recognized his talent, reported him to court, and he was promoted to compiler at the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 遷從仕郎、應奉翰林文字，兼太常博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman and Hanlin Drafting Secretary, concurrently Erudite of the Grand Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman and Hanlin Drafting Secretary, and also served as Erudite of the Grand Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 一時典冊，多出其手。

translations.literal: Canonical documents of the time often issued from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the period's state documents came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，持節使高麗，還，稱旨，授承事郎、山東東西道勸農副使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan he served as envoy bearing the imperial insignia to Goryeo; on return his performance pleased the Emperor, and he was appointed Gentleman for Administrative Service and Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture of the Eastern and Western Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1270 he was sent as envoy to Goryeo. On his return the Emperor was pleased and appointed him Gentleman for Administrative Service and Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture of eastern and western Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丞相伯顏將兵伐宋。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Chancellor Bayan led troops to attack Song.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 Chancellor Bayan led an army against Song.

sentences.zh: 詔選宿望博學、可贊畫大計者與俱行，遂授祺承直郎、行省諮議。

translations.literal: An edict selected men of long-standing reputation and broad learning who could assist in planning the great strategy to go together; Qi was thereupon appointed Gentleman for Direct Service and Counselor of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for men of stature and learning who could help plan the grand campaign. Qi was appointed Gentleman for Direct Service and Counselor of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷郎中，伯顏雅信任之。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Director; Bayan greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to Director, and Bayan trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時軍書填塞，祺酬應剖決，略無凝滯。

translations.literal: At the time military documents piled up; Qi responded and decided them with scarcely any delay.
translations.idiomatic: Military dispatches piled up, but Qi handled and decided them without apparent delay.

sentences.zh: 師駐建康，伯顏以兵事詣闕，政無大小，祺與執政並裁決之。

translations.literal: The army encamped at Jiankang; Bayan went to court on military affairs, and whether policy was great or small, Qi together with the chief ministers decided it.
translations.idiomatic: When the army encamped at Jiankang, Bayan went to court on military business. Qi and the chief ministers decided all affairs, large and small.

sentences.zh: 及戰焦山，宋軍下流。

translations.literal: When battle was joined at Jiaoshan, the Song army drifted downstream.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Jiaoshan the Song forces were driven downstream.

sentences.zh: 祺曰：「不若乘勢速進，以奪彼氣。」

translations.literal: Qi said, "Better to seize the momentum and advance swiftly, to seize their fighting spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "Better to press the advantage and advance at once—to break their spirit."

sentences.zh: 如其言，遂大破之。

translations.literal: As he said, they thereupon routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: They did as he advised and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 伯顏聞之，喜曰：「不意書生乃能知兵若是！」

translations.literal: Bayan heard of it and said with delight, "I never expected a mere scholar could understand warfare like this!"
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan heard of it he exclaimed, "Who would have thought a scholar could know warfare so well!"

sentences.zh: 諸將利虜掠，爭趨臨安，伯顏問計，祺對曰：「宋人之計，惟有竄閩爾。

translations.literal: The generals coveted plunder and raced toward Lin'an; Bayan asked for counsel. Qi replied, "The Song's plan can only be to flee to Min.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, eager for plunder, pressed toward Lin'an. Bayan asked his advice, and Qi replied, "The Song can only intend to flee into Min.

sentences.zh: 若以兵迫之，彼必速逃，一旦盜起臨安，三百年之積，焚蕩無遺矣。

translations.literal: If we press them with troops they will certainly flee quickly; once bandits arise in Lin'an, three hundred years of accumulation will be burned and swept away without remnant.
translations.idiomatic: If we press them with troops they will flee at once, and if raiders then rise in Lin'an, three hundred years of accumulated wealth will be burned to nothing.

sentences.zh: 莫若以計安之，令彼不懼，正如取果，稍待時日耳。」

translations.literal: Better to reassure them with stratagem so they do not fear—as when picking fruit, one need only wait a little time."
translations.idiomatic: Better to reassure them by strategy, so that they do not panic—it is like picking fruit: one need only wait a little longer."

sentences.zh: 伯顏曰：「汝言正合吾意。」

translations.literal: Bayan said, "Your words exactly match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan said, "That is exactly what I mean."

sentences.zh: 乃草書，遣人至臨安，以安慰之，宋乃不復議遷閩。

translations.literal: He thereupon drafted a letter and sent a man to Lin'an to reassure them; Song therefore no longer deliberated on fleeing to Min.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a letter and sent a messenger to Lin'an to reassure them, and Song abandoned talk of fleeing into Min.

sentences.zh: 先是，宋降表稱姪，稱皇帝，屢拒不納。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Song surrender memorial addressed the Yuan as "Nephew" and as "Emperor"; it was repeatedly rejected and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Song surrender memorial had styled the Yuan as "Nephew" and as "Emperor," terms that had been repeatedly rejected.

sentences.zh: 祺自請為使，徵降表。

translations.literal: Qi volunteered to serve as envoy to demand the surrender memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Qi volunteered to go as envoy and demand a surrender memorial in acceptable form.

sentences.zh: 至則會宋相于三省。

translations.literal: On arrival he met with Song chief ministers at the Three Secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he met the Song chief ministers at the Three Secretariats.

sentences.zh: 夜三鼓，議未決，祺正色曰：「國勢至此，夫復何待！」

translations.literal: At the third watch of night deliberation was still unsettled; Qi with stern expression said, "The state's condition has come to this—what more is there to wait for!"
translations.idiomatic: At the third watch of the night the court still had not decided. Qi said sternly, "The state has come to this—what is there left to wait for?"

sentences.zh: 遂定議。

translations.literal: Thereupon the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The decision was then made.

sentences.zh: 書成，宋謝太后內批用寶，攜之以出，復起謝太后於內殿，取國璽十二枚出。

translations.literal: When the document was complete, Empress Dowager Xie affixed an inner endorsement and applied the seal; Qi carried it out. He again summoned Empress Dowager Xie in the inner hall and took out twelve imperial seals of state.
translations.idiomatic: When the document was written, Empress Dowager Xie affixed her inner endorsement and the seal; Qi carried it out. He had the empress dowager rise again in the inner hall and brought out twelve imperial seals of state.

sentences.zh: 伯顏將親封之，祺止之曰：「管鑰自有主者，非所宜親，一有不謹，恐異時姦人妄相染污，終不可明。」

translations.literal: Bayan was about to seal them personally; Qi stopped him, saying, "The keys and seals have their own custodians—it is not appropriate to handle them personally. One lapse of care, and I fear that in later times wicked men may falsely tamper with them and the truth will never be clear."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was about to seal them himself. Qi stopped him: "Custody of the seals has its own officers—it is not proper for you to handle them. One careless act, and later a rogue could tamper with them and the truth would never be clear."

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: He therefore desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan desisted.

sentences.zh: 江南平，伯顏奏祺前後功多，且言祺可任重。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, Bayan memorialized that Qi's merits before and after were many, and further stated that Qi could bear heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified, Bayan memorialized on Qi's many services and said that Qi could shoulder great responsibility.

sentences.zh: 有旨褒陞，授少中大夫、嘉興路緫管，佩虎符。

translations.literal: An edict praised and promoted him; he was appointed Junior Central Grand Master and administrator of Jiaxing Circuit, bearing the tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended and promoted him. He was appointed Junior Central Grand Master and administrator of Jiaxing Circuit with the tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 祺至，首以興學為務，創立規制。

translations.literal: When Qi arrived, he made promoting schools his first task and established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On taking up his post Qi made promoting schools his first priority and established new regulations.

sentences.zh: 在官未久，竟以疾解官，歸東平。

translations.literal: He had not long been in office when he resigned on account of illness and returned to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He had not long been in office when illness forced him to resign and return to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 至元十八年，擢太中大夫、浙東海右道提刑按察使，疾不赴。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace and Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of the Eastern Zhe and Haixi Circuit; illness prevented him from taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace and Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of eastern Zhe and Haixi, but illness kept him from taking up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈宣忠安遠功臣、中奉大夫、參知政事、護軍、魯郡公，諡文襄。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister Loyal in Propagating Worth and Pacifying the Distant, Grand Master for Court Audience, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Defender of the Army, Duke of Lu Commandery, with posthumous name Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister Loyal in Propagating Worth and Pacifying the Distant, Grand Master for Court Audience, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Defender of the Army, and Duke of Lu, with the posthumous name Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 子二人：遵，遹。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Zun and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zun and Yu.

sentences.zh: 閻復字子靖，其先平陽和州人。

translations.literal: Yan Fu, courtesy name Zijing, his ancestors were men of Hezhou in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Fu, courtesy name Zijing, came from a Hezhou family in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 祖衍，仕金，歿王事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan served the Jin and died in the king's service.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan served the Jin and died in its service.

sentences.zh: 父忠，避兵山東之高唐，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father Zhong fled warfare to Gaotang in Shandong and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhong fled the warfare to Gaotang in Shandong and settled there.

sentences.zh: 復始生，有奇光照室。

translations.literal: When Fu was first born, strange light filled the room.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth strange light filled the room.

sentences.zh: 性簡重，美丰儀。

translations.literal: In nature he was austere and dignified, with fine and imposing bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was reserved and dignified, with a striking presence.

sentences.zh: 七歲讀書，穎悟絕人，弱冠入東平學，師事名儒康曄。

translations.literal: At seven he read books, surpassing others in sharp insight; in his early twenties he entered the Dongping academy and studied under the renowned Confucian Kang Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He began reading at seven and was brilliantly quick beyond his peers. In his early twenties he entered the Dongping academy and studied under the renowned scholar Kang Ye.

sentences.zh: 時嚴實領東平行臺，招諸生肄進士業，迎元好問校試其文，預選者四人，復為首，徐琰、李謙、孟祺次之。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Shi headed the Dongping regional office, recruited students to pursue jinshi studies, and invited Yuan Haowen to examine and test their compositions; four men were preselected—Fu ranked first, followed by Xu Yan, Li Qian, and Meng Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi then headed the Dongping regional office, enrolled students for jinshi studies, and invited Yuan Haowen to judge their essays. Four men were chosen—Fu ranked first, followed by Xu Yan, Li Qian, and Meng Qi.

sentences.zh: 歲己未，始掌書記於行臺，擢御史掾。

translations.literal: In the jiwei year he first served as chief secretary at the regional office and was promoted to censorate aide.
translations.idiomatic: In 1259 he first served as chief secretary at the regional office and was promoted to censorate aide.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，用王磐薦，為翰林應奉，以才選充會同館副使，兼接伴使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, through Wang Pan's recommendation, he became Hanlin Attendant; by merit he was selected as deputy commissioner of the Reception Hall and concurrently escort commissioner for visiting envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In 1271, on Wang Pan's recommendation, he became Hanlin Attendant and, by virtue of his talent, was made deputy commissioner of the Reception Hall and escort commissioner for visiting envoys.

sentences.zh: 扈駕上京，賦應制詩二篇，寓規諷意，世祖顧和禮霍孫曰：「有才如此，何可不用！」

translations.literal: Escorting the imperial procession to Shangdu, he composed two court-response poems with admonitory intent. Kublai turned to Helihuo Sun and said, "With talent like this, how can he not be used!"
translations.idiomatic: While escorting the court to Shangdu he composed two imperially commissioned poems with admonitory undertones. Kublai turned to Helihuo Sun and said, "Talent like this—how can we fail to use him!"

sentences.zh: 十二年，陞翰林修撰。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 he was promoted to Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出僉河北河南道提刑按察司事，階奉訓大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out to serve as administrator of the Hebei-Henan Provincial Surveillance Commission, with rank Grand Master for Further Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 he was sent out as administrator of the Hebei-Henan Provincial Surveillance Commission with the rank of Grand Master for Further Instruction.

sentences.zh: 十六年，入為翰林直學士，以州郡校官多不職，建議定銓選之法。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he entered court as Hanlin Direct Academician; because prefectural and district school officers were often negligent in duty, he proposed fixing the selection-and-appointment method.
translations.idiomatic: In 1279 he returned to court as Hanlin Direct Academician. Finding that many local school officers neglected their duties, he proposed fixed standards for appointment.

sentences.zh: 十九年，陞侍講學士，明年，改集賢侍講學士，同領會同館事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Lecturing Academician; the next year he was changed to Lecturing Academician of Scholarly Worthies and jointly directed Reception Hall affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1282 he was promoted to Lecturing Academician; the following year he became Lecturing Academician of Scholarly Worthies and jointly directed the Reception Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，陞翰林學士，帝屢召至榻前，面諭詔旨，具草以進，帝稱善。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to Hanlin Academician; the Emperor repeatedly summoned him before the couch, orally instructing him on edicts; he would draft and submit, and the Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1286 he was promoted to Hanlin Academician. The Emperor repeatedly summoned him to his couch to dictate edicts; Fu drafted them for submission, and the Emperor praised his work.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，尚書省罷，復立中書省，帝勵精圖治，急於擇相，一日，召入便殿，諭之曰：「朕欲命卿執政，何如﹖」復屢謝不足勝任，帝謂侍臣曰：「書生識義理，存謙讓，是也，勿強。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Ministry Secretariat was abolished and the Secretariat was restored; the Emperor strove to govern diligently and was urgent in choosing a chancellor. One day he summoned Fu to the private hall and instructed him, saying, "I wish to appoint you to administer the government—what do you think?" Fu repeatedly declined saying he was not equal to the task. The Emperor told attending ministers, "This scholar understands principle and preserves humility—that is right; do not press him."
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 the Ministry Secretariat was abolished and the Secretariat restored. The Emperor was bent on diligent governance and eager to choose a chancellor. One day he summoned Fu to the private hall and said, "I wish to appoint you chancellor—what do you think?" Fu repeatedly demurred as unqualified. The Emperor told his attendants, "This scholar understands duty and keeps his humility—that is as it should be; do not press him."

sentences.zh: 御史臺改提刑按察司為肅政廉訪司，首命復為浙西道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: The Censorate changed the Surveillance Commission into the Commission for the Promotion of Integrity, and Fu was first appointed Surveillance Commissioner for the Promotion of Integrity of the Zhexi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate renamed the surveillance offices the Commission for the Promotion of Integrity, and Yan Fu was first appointed integrity commissioner for Zhexi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 先是，姦臣桑哥當國，嘗有旨命翰林撰桑哥輔政碑，桑哥既敗，詔有司踣其碑，復等亦坐是免官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the treacherous minister Sangge held the state, there had been an order for the Hanlin to compose a stele on Sangge's assisting governance; after Sangge fell, an edict ordered officials to overturn the stele, and Fu and others were also dismissed from office on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the corrupt minister Sangge dominated the government, the Hanlin had been ordered to compose a stele praising his rule. After Sangge's fall the court had the stele overturned, and Yan Fu and others lost their posts for their part in it.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗即位，以舊臣召入朝，賜重錦、玉環、白金，除集賢學士，階正議大夫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year [1298], when Chengzong took the throne, he was summoned to court as a former minister, granted heavy brocade, a jade ring, and white silver, appointed Academician of Scholarly Worthies, and ranked as Grand Master for Discussion of Governance.
translations.idiomatic: In 1298, when Chengzong succeeded, Yan Fu was recalled as a veteran official and given rich brocade, a jade ring, and silver. He was made Academician of Scholarly Worthies with the rank of Grand Master for Discussion of Governance.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，上疏言：「京師宜首建宣聖廟學，定用釋奠雅樂。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen [1295], he submitted a memorial saying: "The capital should first establish the Temple-School of the Sage of Manifest Culture and fix the use of elegant music for the sacrificial offering."
translations.idiomatic: In 1295 he memorialized: "The capital should lead the realm in building Confucius's temple-school and institute proper ceremonial music for the offering rites."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「曲阜守塚戶，昨有司併入民籍，宜復之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The grave-keeping households at Qufu were yesterday merged by officials into the common subject registers—they should be restored."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the grave-keeping households at Qufu, recently reclassified as ordinary taxpayers, be restored to their former status."

sentences.zh: 其後詔賜孔林洒掃二十八戶、祀田五千畝，皆復之請也。

translations.literal: Later an edict granted twenty-eight households to sweep and sprinkle at the Kong forest and five thousand mu of sacrificial fields—all from Fu's requests for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court granted twenty-eight households to maintain the Kong family grove and five thousand mu of sacrificial land—all at his request.

sentences.zh: 三年，因星變，又上疏言「定律令，頒封贈，增俸給，通調內外官」。

translations.literal: In the third year, because of a change in the stars, he again submitted a memorial speaking of "fixing laws and ordinances, issuing enfeoffments and posthumous grants, increasing salary provisions, and harmonizing appointments of inner and outer officials."
translations.idiomatic: In 1297, citing an ominous change in the heavens, he memorialized again to codify laws, regulate enfeoffments and posthumous honors, raise salaries, and standardize appointments at court and in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「古者，刑不上大夫，今郡守以徵租受杖，非所以厲廉隅。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "In antiquity punishment did not reach great officers; today prefects are flogged for collecting taxes—this is not how to encourage integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "In antiquity punishment did not touch high officials, yet today prefects are beaten for tax collection—that does not encourage integrity.

sentences.zh: 江南公田租重，宜減，以貸貧民。」

translations.literal: Public-field rents in the south of the Yangzi are heavy and should be reduced to lend relief to poor people."
translations.idiomatic: Public-field rents in the south are too heavy and should be cut to relieve the poor."

sentences.zh: 後多采用。

translations.literal: Many of these were later adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his proposals were later adopted.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，仍遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade [1297] he was again transferred to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In 1297 he was again made Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔賜楮幣萬貫。

translations.literal: In the second year an edict bestowed ten thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In 1298 the emperor granted him ten thousand strings of paper currency.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝召至榻前，密諭之曰：「中書庶務繁重，左相難其人，卿為朕舉所知。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor summoned him before the couch and secretly instructed him: "The Central Secretariat's routine affairs are heavy; a left chancellor is hard to find—recommend someone you know to Us."
translations.idiomatic: In 1300 the emperor called him to the couch and said privately, "The Secretariat's business is overwhelming and I cannot find a left chancellor—recommend someone you trust."

sentences.zh: 復以哈剌哈孫對。

translations.literal: Fu answered with Harghasun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Fu named Harghasun.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，即遣使召入，相之；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, immediately sent envoys to summon him in, and made him chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, summoned Harghasun at once, and made him chancellor;

sentences.zh: 復亦拜翰林學士承旨，階正奉大夫。

translations.literal: Fu was also appointed Hanlin Expositor-in-Chief, rank Grand Master of Positive Service.
translations.idiomatic: and Yan Fu was promoted to Hanlin Expositor-in-Chief with the rank of Grand Master of Positive Service.
